member.summary: Number of performed iterations. Only set on the solution returned by Solve, zero on all others.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution.random
member.summary: Random generator used to create random solutions. It is shared by all solutions and seeded with a fixed value, so a sequence of runs always gives the same start solutions.

Lowest value of a vector component.
Highest value of a vector component.
The function to minimize.
Caller data passed on to the objective function. Can be null.

The function to minimize.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution.ToString

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.maxX
member.summary: Highest value of a vector component in the start solutions. Note that it only seeds the start amoeba and is _not_ enforced while solving.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.alpha
member.summary: Reflection factor, set to 1.0 by the constructor.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.beta
member.summary: Contraction factor, set to 0.5 by the constructor.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.gamma
member.summary: Expansion factor, set to 2.0 by the constructor.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.maxLoop
member.summary: Maximum number of iterations of the main loop in Solve.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.stopval
member.summary: Value to stop at. Solve stops when the best solution has a smaller value than this, which is an absolute value and _not_ a tolerance on the size of the amoeba.

member.summary: Caller data passed on to the objective function at every evaluation. Can be null.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.Centroid
member.summary: Helper function to Solve which computes the centroid of all solutions except the worst one. The reflection, expansion and contraction steps are all measured from this point.
member.returns: A new solution holding the centroid vector and its computed value.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.Reflected(IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution)
member.summary: Helper function to Solve which mirrors the worst solution through the centroid, scaled with alpha.
member.param: The centroid of all solutions except the worst one.
member.returns: A new solution holding the reflected vector and its computed value.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.Expanded(IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution,IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution)
member.summary: Helper function to Solve which reaches further out from the centroid, past the reflected point, scaled with gamma.
member.param: The reflected solution to reach past.
The centroid of all solutions except the worst one.
member.returns: A new solution holding the expanded vector and its computed value.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.Contracted(IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution)
member.summary: Helper function to Solve which moves the worst solution towards the centroid, scaled with beta, but never past the centroid.
member.param: The centroid of all solutions except the worst one.
member.returns: A new solution holding the contracted vector and its computed value.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.Shrink
member.summary: Helper function to Solve which moves all solutions except the best one in-place halfway towards the best solution. Note that the values are computed again and that the amoeba is sorted after.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.ReplaceWorst(IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution)
member.summary: Helper function to Solve which replaces the worst solution of the amoeba in-place with a given solution. Note that the vector is copied, so newSolution is left untouched, and that the amoeba is sorted after.
member.param: The solution to copy over the worst one.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.IsWorseThanAllButWorst(IGS.Genamo.AmoebaSolution)
member.summary: Checks if a reflected solution is worse, that is has a larger value, than all solutions of the amoeba except the worst one. Solve uses this to decide if the amoeba should be contracted.
member.param: The reflected solution to check.
member.returns: true if the reflected solution is worse than all solutions but the worst one, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.Solve
member.summary: Performs the main loop, which reflects, expands, contracts and shrinks the amoeba in-place until the best value is smaller than stopval or maxLoop iterations are done. Note that the loop stops on an absolute value and _not_ on the size of the amoeba.
member.returns: The best solution, which is always the one at index 0. Iterations is set on it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.AmoebaOptimizer.ToString
member.summary: Returns a new string containing debug purpose info, with one line per solution of the amoeba prefixed by its index.
member.returns: A string with data for all solutions of the amoeba.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Apollonius2d.SolveLinePoint(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double[],System.Double[],System.Double[])
member.summary: Computes the circles with a given radius that tangent a line and pass through a point. Both sides of the line are tried, so up to four solutions can be found. The computation is done along x or along y depending on which avoids a division by zero.
member.param: The radius of the circles to compute.
X of the start point of the line. The line is considered infinite.
Y of the start point of the line.
X of the end point of the line.
Y of the end point of the line.
X coordinate of the point.
Y coordinate of the point.
Receives the center x of each solution circle. The array must have room for eight values.
Receives the center y of each solution circle.
Receives the radius of each solution circle, which is always r0.
member.returns: The number of solutions found, or 0 if the point is further from the line than 2*r0.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Apollonius2d.SolvePointPoint(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double[],System.Double[],System.Double[])
member.summary: Computes the circles with a given radius that pass through two points. There are two solutions, one on each side of the line between the points, one when the points are exactly 2*r0 apart and none when they are further apart than that. The computation is done along x or along y depending on which avoids a division by zero.
member.param: The radius of the circles to compute.
X coordinate of the first point.
Y coordinate of the first point.
X coordinate of the second point.
Y coordinate of the second point.
Receives the center x of each solution circle. The array must have room for two values.
Receives the center y of each solution circle.
Receives the radius of each solution circle, which is always r0.
member.returns: The number of solutions found, which is 0, 1 or 2.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Arc2d
member.summary: Class describing a circular arc. This circular arc should not be seen as a part of a circle, but more lika a bent segment. Internally it is stored with two points and a bulge factor, which makes it possible to have an arc that equals a line segment. The bulge is defined as i=4*atan(bulge) where i is the arcs included angle. A positive bulge is a counter clockwise arc while a negative is a clockwise.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Arc2d.bulge
member.summary: The bulge factor of the arc, defined as tan(i/4) where i is the included angle. A positive bulge gives a counter clockwise arc, a negative a clockwise one, and a bulge of zero a line segment.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d
member.summary:
Class used by Poly2d to optimize a polygon.
The arc engine () is a tolerance-band fitter: the result poly is guaranteed to stay within tol of the input everywhere. It works in three stages:
0. Corner pre-pass - turning-angle breakpoints split the poly into smooth runs so no fitted primitive ever spans a corner (this is what stops corner cutting, independently of tol). 1. Per-span fit - an algebraic (Kasa) circle seed, constrained to pass exactly through the two span endpoints (G0 watertight), then an *exact* max-deviation test (segment endpoints + the clamped perpendicular foot of the centre - the only three points where |dist-r| can peak on a straight sub-edge). No sampling gaps. 2. Segmentation - greedy longest primitive per step, found by exponential march + bisection. O(n log n)-ish. The committed primitive is always re-verified, so non-monotone fitness can only cost a segment, never the tolerance.
Precondition: the input is expected to be line-only (Poly2d.ArcFit runs LineFit first). The exact deviation test assumes straight sub-edges.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d.DefaultCornerAngleRad
member.summary: Vertices turning more than this are treated as hard corners (never spanned).

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d.Compute(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Optimizes a poly with arc (and line) segments, staying within .
member.param: Input poly (line-only; arcs should be flattened upstream).
Maximum allowed deviation of the result from the input.
Turning angle (radians) above which a vertex is kept as a corner.

0..1 trade of edge count for tangent smoothness. 0 = fastest greedy (longest valid arc per step, today's behaviour). Above 0 a tangent-aware DP places breakpoints to minimise edgeCount + quality*(total tangent mismatch in degrees), so it spends edges to remove the C0 kinks greedy leaves at curvature transitions. quality is scale- and tol-invariant.
member.returns: An arc-fitted poly.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d.FitRunDP(IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d.FitCtx,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Double,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Double})
member.summary: Tangent-aware segmentation of a run. Shortest-path DP over tol-valid primitives that minimises edgeCount + lambda*(sum of tangent mismatch, radians) at interior joints. The hard tolerance constraint still comes from LineFits/ArcFits, so nothing leaves the band. Because a segment is penalised where its fitted end-tangent diverges from the data tangent, breakpoints migrate onto real curvature transitions (big radius / small radius / line), which is where consecutive arcs then meet tangentially - killing the C0 kinks.

member.summary: Checks if the part of the run from i to j stays within the tolerance of the straight chord between its endpoints. The distance is measured to the chord as a segment, so a point beyond an endpoint is measured to that endpoint.
member.param: The node coordinates and the tolerance to fit within.
Node indices of the run, in travel order.
Index in the run of the first node of the span.
Index in the run of the last node of the span.
member.returns: true if a line is within the tolerance, otherwise false. A zero length chord, which happens at the seam of a closed poly, is never accepted as a line.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d.ArcFits(IGS.Genamo.ArcFit2d.FitCtx,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Double@)
member.summary: Checks if the part of the run from i to j can be replaced by a single arc within the tolerance, and computes the bulge of that arc. The center comes from an algebraic Kasa fit which is then projected onto the perpendicular bisector of the two endpoints, so the arc passes exactly through them and the result stays watertight. Every straight sub-edge is tested at both its endpoints and at the clamped perpendicular foot of the center, which are the only places where the distance to the circle can peak. The arc is also rejected when the data sweeps more than half a circle around the center, or when the sweep is not monotone, since a point can lie on the circle without lying on the arc.
member.param: The node coordinates and the tolerance to fit within.
Node indices of the run, in travel order.
Index in the run of the first node of the span.
Index in the run of the last node of the span.
Set to the bulge of the fitted arc, positive for a counter clockwise arc and negative for a clockwise one, or to 0.0 when no arc fits.
member.returns: true if an arc within the tolerance was found, otherwise false. Coinciding endpoints and colinear points give false, since the line path handles those.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.FlattenArc(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.LinkList{System.Double},IGS.Genamo.LinkListNode{System.Double})
member.summary: Recursively subdivides the parameter interval par1 to par2 until an arc through the interval can represent the curve within acc, inserting the parameter of every subdivision into res so that the list stays sorted. The candidate arc is built through the start, mid and end point of the interval and is measured against two further samples inside it: the mid and quarter point when the arc degenerates to a straight chord, the quarter and three quarter point otherwise. The interval is accepted and the recursion stops when both samples are within acc. The recursion has no depth limit, so an acc of zero or less does not terminate.
member.param: Start parameter of the interval to subdivide.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.Flatten(System.Double)
member.summary: Flattens the curve into an open polyline of straight segments that stays within tol of the curve. The parameter range is split recursively at its midpoint until the chord between the interval end points is within tol of both the mid and the quarter point of that interval, and the sampled points are added to the polyline in order from start to end. The polyline always holds at least the start and the end point of the curve, so a curve whose control points all coincide gives a two point polyline of zero length. Subdivision is not depth limited, so a tol of zero or less does not terminate. Use ArcFit instead when arcs rather than straight segments are wanted.
member.param: Largest allowed deviation between the polyline and the curve.
member.returns: A new open polyline of straight segments approximating the curve.

member.summary: Recursively subdivides the parameter interval par1 to par2 until the straight chord between its end points is within acc of the curve, inserting the point at every subdivision parameter into res so that the list stays sorted. Both the mid and the quarter point of the interval are measured against the chord, which catches the symmetric case where the mid point happens to fall on the chord. The recursion has no depth limit, so an acc of zero or less does not terminate.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.CreateFromArc(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d)
member.summary: Creates the bezier curves that approximate an arc. A linear arc gives a single bezier whose control points are the chord sampled at one third and two thirds, which represents the straight segment exactly. A curved arc is divided into as few equal segments of at most a quarter turn as its sweep angle needs, and each segment gets the control point offset that matches the circle to a few parts per million of the radius. The direction of the arc is kept. An arc that is not linear but still has a sweep angle of zero gives an empty list.
member.param: The arc to convert.
member.returns: The bezier curves representing the arc, in order from start to end, or an empty list.

The parameter is clamped to the range 0 to 1 first, so a t outside that range splits at the nearest end and returns one degenerate curve with all four control points at that end point together with a copy of the whole curve.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.Distance(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes the distance from a point to the closest point on the curve. The curve is treated as a bounded segment, so a point whose nearest projection falls outside the parameter range 0 to 1 gets the distance to the nearer end point. The result carries the numeric accuracy of ClosestPoint, which finds its candidate parameters to about 1e-6.
member.param: The point from which the distance is calculated.
member.returns: The distance from the point to the curve.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.ToRegion(System.Double)
member.summary: Converts the curve to a region holding a single arc fitted polyline that stays within tol of the curve. The polyline is open and encloses no area, so the region is a wire rather than a filled shape.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.ClosestPoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes the point on the curve closest to a given point. The candidate parameters are the real roots of the fifth degree polynomial that vanishes where the squared distance is stationary, solved numerically to an accuracy of 1e-6 in at most 50 iterations, and only roots inside the parameter range 0 to 1 are used. Both end points are compared as well, so the result is always on the curve segment and a curve with no usable root falls back to the nearer end point. The returned point is always a new object, never one of the control points of the curve.
member.param: The point to find the closest curve point to.
member.returns: A new point on the curve closest to the given point.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.ParamsAt(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Returns all parameters at a given point.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.Length
member.summary: Gets the arc length of the curve. There is no closed form for a cubic, so the magnitude of the analytic derivative is integrated over the parameter range 0 to 1 with Simpson's rule. The integration refines until two successive estimates agree to within a relative tolerance of Calc.Epsilon, which normally takes far fewer than the 1024 refinements allowed, and throws "Numeric integration failed to converge" if that limit is reached. A curve whose control points all coincide integrates to zero and converges at once.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.Tangent(System.Double)
member.summary: Computes the tangent direction of the curve at parameter t, as a plane angle in radians normalised to the range 0 up to but not including two PI. The angle is taken from the line between the point at t on the line from the start point to the point at t on P1 to P2, and the point at t on the line from that point to the end point. This is exact at t equal to 0, where it is the direction from P0 to P1, and at t equal to 1, where it is the direction from P2 to P3, but it is only an approximation in between and can differ from the true tangent by tens of degrees on a strongly curved span. Coincident control points can leave the underlying line degenerate, in which case the angle is zero.
member.param: The parameter between 0 and 1 to take the tangent at.
member.returns: The tangent angle in radians in the range 0 up to two PI.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Bezier2d.TangentsAt(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Returns all tangent angles at a given point.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FitBezierCurves.FitCurve(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Double,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d})
member.summary: Fits a cubic bezier curve to a list of digitized points within the given tolerance, appending the resulting control points to result. The unit tangents at the two ends are estimated from the first and the last pair of points, and the fit itself is delegated to FitCubic. Only the second, third and fourth control point of each fitted segment are appended, so the start point d[0] is never added and has to be supplied by the caller. At least two points are required; with zero or one point the tangent estimation indexes outside d and an IndexOutOfRangeException is thrown.
member.param: The digitized points to fit, in curve order.
The fitting tolerance, compared against the largest squared distance from a point to the fitted curve.
The list the control points are appended to; the list is mutated, not replaced.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FitBezierCurves.FitCubic(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Int32,System.Int32,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,System.Double,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d})
member.summary: Fits one cubic bezier to the points d[first] to d[last] with the two end tangents held fixed, and appends its second, third and fourth control point to result. A range of exactly two points is handled by the heuristic of placing both inner control points one third of the chord length out along the tangents. Otherwise the points are chord length parameterized, a curve is generated, and the largest squared deviation is measured; if it is below error the curve is accepted. If it is below error squared the parameters are refined by up to forty Newton-Raphson reparameterization passes, each followed by a new fit. The recursive split at the point of maximum error, which is what the original algorithm does when the tolerance cannot be met, is commented out in this port, so a failed fit appends its last curve anyway and the routine always produces exactly one segment and never recurses.

The index in d of the first point of the range.
The index in d of the last point of the range.
The unit tangent at the start of the range, pointing forwards into the curve.
The unit tangent at the end of the range, pointing backwards into the curve.
The fitting tolerance, compared against the largest squared distance from a point to the fitted curve.
The list the control points are appended to; the list is mutated, not replaced.

member.summary: Solves for the two inner control points of a cubic bezier whose end points are pinned to d[first] and d[last] and whose end tangent directions are given, using the least squares system of the original algorithm. The two distances along the tangents are obtained from the determinants of a two by two matrix; when that matrix is singular, or either distance comes out smaller than a millionth of the chord length, the Wu and Barsky fallback of one third of the chord length is used instead, which avoids the coincident control points that would divide by zero in a later Newton-Raphson step. uPrime must hold one parameter for every point in the range. A new array is returned; none of the arguments are modified.

The index in d of the first point of the range.
The index in d of the last point of the range.

The unit tangent at the start of the range, pointing forwards into the curve.
The unit tangent at the end of the range, pointing backwards into the curve.

member.summary: Improves one parameter value by a single Newton-Raphson step, moving u towards the parameter at which the cubic Q comes closest to P. The control points of the first and second derivative curves are built from Q and evaluated by de Casteljau. member.summary: Approximates the unit tangent at an interior point of a digitized curve by averaging the direction from d[center] back to the previous point with the direction from the next point back to d[center], then normalizing, so the result points backwards along the curve and has to be negated to serve as the start tangent of the following segment. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BSweep.Intersect(IGS.Genamo.BSweep.BSweepNode,IGS.Genamo.BSweep.BSweepNode,IGS.Genamo.Point2d@)
member.summary: Finds one intersection between the arcs of two events. Endpoints of one arc that lie on the other arc are tested first, then a general arc against arc intersection is done. A point that falls on an endpoint of both arcs is not reported, since the arcs already meet there and splitting would produce a zero length piece. All comparisons are done on the fixed point grid, so points closer than one grid step count as the same point.
member.param: The event of the arc being swept in.
The event of an arc taken from the active edge list.
Receives the intersection point. Only meaningful when the result is not NoIntersection.
member.returns: IntersectOnA when only the first arc has to be split, IntersectOnB when only the second arc has to be split, both flags when the point splits both arcs, and NoIntersection when the arcs do not cross away from their endpoints.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BSweep.Compute(IGS.Genamo.Boolean2dProgressDelegate)
member.summary: Runs the sweep and returns the arcs split at every point where they crossed each other. The event list is sorted once and then worked off from bottom to top. An add node is first made Y-monotone, then tested against every arc in the active edge list, and each arc that is found to intersect is erased together with its events and replaced by two new arcs that are inserted as new events; an arc that hits nothing is put into the active edge list. A deletion node only removes its partner from the active edge list again. The event list is consumed, so the sweep should not be reused after this call. The progress callback is called for about every hundredth event and is handed the number of events still left, not a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0.
member.param: Callback for progress reporting, or null for no reporting.
member.returns: The split arcs. Tag and set of an original arc are carried over to all its pieces.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BSweep.MakeYMonotone(IGS.Genamo.BSweep.BSweepNode)
member.summary: Splits the arc of an event at the topmost or bottommost point of its circle so that the arc becomes Y-monotone, which the sweep depends on since it represents every arc by the lower left and the upper right corner of its bounding box. Linear arcs, and arcs that do not pass such an extreme point away from their endpoints, are left alone, and the split is also skipped when one of the two pieces would come out shorter than 1e-5. When the arc is split the original arc and both its events are erased and the two pieces are inserted instead, so the caller must drop the event it passed in.
member.param: The add node whose arc is checked.
member.returns: true if the arc was split and replaced, false if it was left unchanged.

Shows a message box naming the problem when a check fails and does nothing at all otherwise. It is not called during normal operation.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Boolean2d.Sweep
member.summary: Sweeps the arcs from bottom to top and keeps only the edges that belong to the result of the boolean operation. Works in place on the arc list, which is replaced by the kept arcs, so the arcs that are thrown away are lost. Two nodes, one add node and one delete node, are created for every arc, sorted with the compare function of the current boolean rule, and then passed one by one to AddToAel which maintains the active edge list. Expects the arcs to be split at all their intersections already, which Compute does with BSweep, and expects the boolean rule to be set, an unset rule gives a null reference exception. An empty arc list simply leaves the list empty.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Boolean2d.AddToAel(IGS.Genamo.BNode,IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.BNode})
member.summary: Inserts an edge in the active edge list and decides if the edge belongs to the result. The list is kept sorted from left to right, the insert position is the first edge that lies to the right of the new edge at its bottom point according to BNode.CompareAel, and the node is linked back from n.ael so that the matching delete node can erase it again. While walking to the insert position the edges passed on the left are counted, once for all edges and once per input set, a leftedge counting up and a rightedge counting down, and those crossing counts are handed to the KeepEdge function of the current boolean rule.
member.param: The edge to insert, taken from the add node of an arc.
The active edge list to insert into, modified in place.
member.returns: True if the edge should be added to the result, false otherwise.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Boolean2d.Join
member.summary: Joins the arcs kept by the sweep into polys and returns them as a new region, the arc list itself is left untouched. The arcs are first joined with Join2d without any tolerance, then every poly that did not come out closed is joined a second time with a tolerance of 1e-3, which repairs chains left dangling by small gaps. Polys that are still open after that are not thrown away, they are appended last, after the closed polys have been normalized, so the caller can filter them out. An empty arc list gives an empty region.
member.returns: A new region with the joined polys, closed polys first and any remaining open polys last.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d
member.summary:
Robust replacement for .
Instead of walking the raw (possibly dirty) geometry and recomputing intersections/angles at every step, this class first builds a *clean planar arrangement* with a single tolerance, then traces faces combinatorially using a half-edge rotational system. All robustness lives in the cleaning stage; the trace itself cannot hang because every directed half-edge belongs to exactly one face cycle and is visited at most once.
Arcs are tessellated into line segments up front, so the entire arrangement runs on lines only. This removes every arc-specific numerical failure mode (huge-radius circle intersections, on-arc tolerance rejections) at the cost of a polyline result, which the caller re-fits to arcs afterward (see ).
Pipeline: 0. Normalize input: tessellate arcs to lines, derive one working tolerance. 1. Build the arrangement: a. weld endpoints (merges near-coincident points) c. dedupe coincident input edges, then bridge dangling ends to close gaps b. split edges at pairwise crossings, with an endpoint-projection catch for crossings that land exactly on a vertex d. drop slivers, dedupe again Gap closing runs BEFORE the crossing pass, so bridges are split like any other geometry and the arrangement is planar by construction. 2. Build half-edges and the per-vertex rotational (CCW) order. 3. Trace every face cycle. 4. Group cycles into faces: every CCW cycle is the outer boundary of one bounded face, every CW cycle is an inner boundary (hole) of exactly one face. Holes are attributed by shooting a -X ray from the cycle's leftmost vertex, then resolving the resulting links with union-find.
Two entry points share stages 0-4: - the single face containing a pick point (+ its holes). - every bounded face of the arrangement.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.input
member.summary: The raw input geometry accumulated by the Add overloads, held as arcs (a line is a zero-bulge arc). Consumed by Build; never modified afterwards.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.RelativeEpsilon
member.summary: Relative tolerance, scaled by the bounding-box diagonal. This is the working/weld tolerance: endpoints closer than this are merged, points within this of an edge split it, and arcs whose sagitta is below it are flattened. 1e-6 of the part size is a realistic CAD merge tolerance; tighten for clean data, loosen for dirtier input.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.AbsoluteEpsilon
member.summary: Absolute tolerance floor, used when the geometry is tiny.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.ToleranceOverride
member.summary: If > 0, overrides the auto-derived working (resolution) tolerance.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.GapTolerance
member.summary:
Gap-closing distance, in drawing units. When larger than the resolution tolerance, dangling (valence-1) endpoints are joined to the nearest vertex or edge within this distance by a short bridge edge, closing breaks and T-gaps in dirty input.
Nothing already in the drawing moves - the bridge is added geometry - so an existing edge can never sweep across other geometry and fabricate a false face. The cost is a small jog of up to this length in the traced boundary. Only free ends are bridged, so distinct connected features are never joined. 0 (or <= resolution) disables it.
This is absolute, not relative: a break is an artifact of the source data and its size has nothing to do with how much geometry happens to be selected.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.ArcChordTolerance
member.summary: Per-segment chord deviation budget when tessellating arcs into line segments. 0 = use a quarter of the working tolerance (keeps the tessellated boundary well inside the weld budget). Larger = fewer segments (coarser arcs).

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.BoundsSwell
member.summary: Amount to swell broadphase query boxes so junctions lost to arc tessellation (and exact touches lost to floating point) still get their pair tested. Negative = auto: the working tolerance, which matches what the narrowphase will actually accept. Anything smaller leaves a dead band where Project would accept a junction that never becomes a candidate. 0 disables swelling. Note this only decides which pairs are *tested* - Project still rejects beyond tol - so a larger swell costs time, not correctness.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.MaxArcSegments

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.Build
member.summary: Builds the planar arrangement and traces all face cycles. Idempotent: repeated calls are free until new geometry is added.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.AssignFaces(System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.Int32,System.Int32}@,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32}}@)
member.summary:
Groups traced cycles into faces. Every CCW cycle is the outer boundary of exactly one bounded face; every CW cycle is an inner boundary of exactly one face (possibly the unbounded one). Cycles are linked by and resolved with union-find, so each component holds exactly one CCW cycle - or the UNBOUNDED sentinel, in which case the component is not a face and is simply never emitted.
Keys in both dictionaries are union-find component roots.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.FindContainer(System.Int32)
member.summary:
Finds the cycle bounding the face that contains cycle , by shooting a -X ray from the cycle's leftmost vertex and taking the first edge strictly to its left. Returns when nothing lies to the left.
The hit may belong to another inner boundary of the same face (two holes side by side), so the caller resolves the links transitively. Because the hit is strictly to the left, the target cycle's leftmost vertex is strictly further left and the link graph is acyclic.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.CycleAtPlusX(System.Int32)
member.summary: The cycle owning the wedge containing direction +X at vertex . Outgoing half-edges are CCW-sorted and the wedge left of half-edge i spans (ang_i, ang_i+1), so direction 0 == 2PI falls in the wedge left of the largest-angle half-edge. (Degenerate case: an outgoing half-edge at angle exactly 0 means the ray is collinear with it; we still take the last, giving the face immediately below that edge.)

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.BuildFace(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32}})
member.summary: Materialises one face: its CCW outer poly plus the CW holes registered against the same component root. Pass null for to build the outer loop only.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.Bridges
member.summary: Debug: the bridge segments added by gap closing, in emission order. Filled during the build; empty when GapTolerance is inactive.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.BridgeGaps(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.Edge},IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.VertexStore,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary:
Closes gaps by adding short bridge edges from dangling (valence-1) endpoints to the nearest vertex or edge point within . Nothing already in the drawing moves: bridges are ordinary edges appended to the list, so the intersection pass that follows splits them - and anything they cross - exactly like any other geometry, and the arrangement stays planar by construction.
This is why bridging is preferred over snapping the endpoint onto the target. Moving a free end rotates its incident edge about the far endpoint, sweeping a triangle as long as the edge; anything inside that triangle silently gains or loses a crossing. A bridge is at most gapTol long, so any face it can fabricate has a side no longer than the gap.
Only free ends are considered, so distinct connected features are never joined. Targets are chosen against a fixed edge set with id tie-breaks and materialised afterwards, so the result does not depend on processing order.

member.param: Start point of the segment.

The point to project.
member.returns: A new point on the segment, closest to p.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.Tessellate(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Arc2d})
member.summary: Expands an arc into one or more line segments (chords), appending them to . Lines pass through unchanged. Arcs that are flat at tolerance, or whose radius is so large that arc math would be numerically unstable, collapse to a single chord. Everything else is tessellated so each segment's deviation from the true arc stays within the chord budget. The whole downstream pipeline then operates on lines only, eliminating every arc-specific numerical failure mode. (Arcs are re-fit to the resulting polyline afterward by the caller.)

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.BuildPoly(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.BoundaryArrangement2d.HEdge},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d})
member.summary: Builds a closed Poly2d from a face cycle, cancelling consecutive reverse pairs. A dangling spur appears as an out/back twin pair that is adjacent in the cycle; the stack cancellation removes it (and nested spurs) so the boundary stays clean. A second pass cancels a spur that straddles the cycle seam, which the linear pass cannot see.

member.summary: Picks which candidate edge the walk should follow next. Each candidate is oriented to start at the end of the incoming arc, and the one making the smallest clockwise turn is taken, so the walk hugs one face. A turn of nearly zero is treated as a full turn instead, which stops the walk doubling straight back on itself. Ties are broken by direction, then by radius or length. A candidate whose end is within sqacc of the start point wins immediately, closing the loop.

member.summary: Finds where a ray meets each of the given arcs and returns the hits sorted from the start of the ray. Besides real crossings it also records near misses: an arc passing within 1e-3 of the ray end, or with an end point within 1e-3 of the ray, counts as a hit. Those thresholds are absolute distances and do not scale with the drawing. Hits at a parameter of Calc.Epsilon or less are dropped, so the ray does not catch on its own start point. member.summary: Computes a new minimal circle when a point is added to a support set holding two points. All circles defined by the new point together with one of the two support points are tested, and the smallest one that encloses the remaining point is used. If no such circle exists the circle through all three points is used instead. The support list is updated in-place to describe the returned circle.

member.summary: Computes a new minimal circle when a point is added to a support set holding three points. Six candidate circles are tested, three defined by the new point and one support point as a diameter, and three defined by the new point and two support points. The smallest candidate that encloses the remaining support points is used. If floating point round-off makes all candidates fail, the candidate with the smallest error is used. The support list is updated in-place to describe the returned circle.
member.param: Index in the point list of the point to add to the support set.
The complete list of points.
Indices of the current support points. Updated in-place.
member.returns: The new minimal circle.

member.summary: Creates a random polygon for testing purposes. It builds shapecnt star shaped polygons with pntcnt vertices each, growing them out from the midpoint of a random edge of an already created shape, unions them all with the clipper boolean union and then scales and translates the first resulting contour to fill the given bounding box exactly. A new Random is created on every call, so the result differs between calls. The vertex placement loop retries until a point falls inside bb, so a degenerate bounding box can loop forever, and an empty union result throws.

member.summary: Clips a line segment against an axis aligned rectangle with the Cohen-Sutherland algorithm. The four coordinates are modified in place to the clipped endpoints, but only when the segment is at least partly visible; if the segment is completely outside the rectangle they are left untouched and false is returned. A segment already completely inside the rectangle is also left untouched and true is returned. Since the clipping is done in a single pass, a segment passing through a corner region can fail the final bounds check and be reported as invisible.

member.summary: Settings for . All distances are in drawing units (mm).

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.FlattenTolerance
member.summary: Tolerance used when flattening arc segments of the input poly.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.SampleSpacing
F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.MaxSamples
member.summary: Upper bound on the number of boundary samples. The spacing is increased if needed. Triangulation is O(n²) in this count, so keep it a few thousand at most.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.PruneFactor
member.summary: Side branches shorter than PruneFactor * (local width at the junction) are removed, as are branches up to twice that length whose median width is under 70% of the junction width (the run-out into a rounded end next to a junction, e.g. a hairpin). Removes the spurious stubs the triangulation creates at end caps and corners. Also removes genuine branches shorter than the width, which is normally what you want.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.TrimFactor
member.summary: The last TrimFactor * width of every free end is discarded and replaced by an extrapolation (circle or line, fitted to the axis just inside the trimmed region) out to the boundary. The triangulation is unreliable within about one width of a cap. Free ends that sit in a rounded cap (an arc of 150° or more with radius ~W/2) are not trimmed this way: the cap centre is used as an exact axis point instead.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.MaxWidth
member.summary: If > 0, the computation fails when an axis has a median width above this, or any measured width above 1.5 × this (junction nodes measure up to ~1.4 × the width). This is a convenience gate; for an exact "thin everywhere" test use OffsetUnion(-MaxWidth/2) on the region and check for emptiness.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.AllowBranches
member.summary: If false, the computation fails when the shape has branches (more than one axis curve after pruning). If true all branches are returned as separate open curves that meet at junction points.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxisSettings.FitTolerance
member.summary: Tolerance for the final DouglasPeucker + ArcFit of each axis. 0 = return the raw polyline of chord midpoints.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxis2d
member.summary:
Computes the centre line ("chordal axis") of a thin closed shape, such as a slit drawn as a closed contour. Works for straight, curved, bent and branched thin shapes of roughly constant width; free ends land on the middle of the end cap.
Method: flatten and resample the boundary, constrained Delaunay triangulation (ear clipping + Lawson flips; no external library), then the chordal axis transform: the axis passes through the interior triangle edges (the "chords" across the shape), at the point equidistant from the two boundary lines in straight-sided regions and at the midpoint elsewhere. Sleeve triangles link two chords, junction triangles branch, terminal triangles end. Spurious short branches are pruned, the unreliable last width of each free end is replaced by a fitted extrapolation out to the boundary, and the result is arc-fitted.
Input: a closed Poly2d, or a Region2d with one outer contour and any number of holes (letters with counters). Holes make the axis graph cyclic: an O gives one closed curve, an A a loop plus two legs. Contours that cross or touch are detected and rejected.

member.summary: Computes the chordal axis of a region: one outer contour and any number of holes, all closed. Orientation is fixed here (outer CCW, holes CW; the largest contour by area is taken as the outer one). Contours must not touch or cross each other.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxis2d.SplicePassThroughJunctions(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxis2d.Node},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32[]})
member.summary: Pass-through junctions (two legs left after pruning) sit off the centre line: at bends, and in small junction regions such as a flat apex. Ones within a width of each other along the graph are treated as one cluster. The cluster is replaced by the intersection of its two external legs (lines or circles) when that point lies ahead of both legs and inside the shape (the sharp corner of an L, a stem meeting a bowl); otherwise every junction in the cluster is bypassed and the chord points are kept (a flat apex whose leg centre lines meet outside the glyph, a stub pruned off a straight run).

member.summary: Nearest point to c on the boundary within 'span' samples either side of sample g.

member.summary: Centre of the maximal disk touching the boundary stretches around the given samples (the medial-axis junction point), by alternating nearest-point and circle-centre steps.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxis2d.ClusterJunctions(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.ChordalAxis2d.Node},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d},System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32[]})
member.summary: Real junctions (three or more legs) connected through short chains (within a width) are one junction: an X at an acute angle is two Y-junctions and a connector in the medial axis, a cross is two triangles sharing a chord. Each cluster becomes one node. Its position is the least-squares intersection of all its legs when that is well conditioned (legs at 30° or more: the sharp T, Y and X), inside the shape and near the cluster; otherwise (a shallow fork such as the waist of a B) the medial-axis point: the centre of the largest disk touching the boundary stretches around the junction triangles' vertices.

member.summary: Initial position of a junction node: the centre of the empty circle through the three boundary vertices of the junction triangle (its circumcentre), which is a medial axis point and symmetric where the shape is. Falls back to the centroid for obtuse triangles, where the circumcentre lies outside the triangle.

member.summary: Computes a new circle which is the best fit to a list of points, minimizing the distance from the points to the circle itself rather than the algebraic error. The fit is iterative, starting from the average of the points, and stops when the center moves less than the tolerance or when the iteration limit is reached. Points closer to the current center than the tolerance are skipped in that step.

The largest center movement that is considered converged.
member.returns: A new circle. Note that the result is returned even when the iteration did not converge.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ClipperBoolean
member.summary: Wrapper that runs boolean operations on Region2d and Poly2d through the Clipper polygon clipping library. The members at the top use Clipper2Lib and work on double coordinates directly. The members below the OLD marker use the older integer based Clipper namespace, where coordinates are multiplied by scale on the way in and divided by it on the way out. All input must be flattened first, since only the node points of a poly are converted and arc bulges are ignored. Every operation returns a new region or poly and never changes its arguments.

member.summary: Region must be flattened

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClipperBoolean.Union(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d)
member.summary: Unions a single poly with itself, which removes self intersections and gives back a clean outline. The poly must be flattened. Returns a new region and leaves the poly untouched.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1
member.summary: Finds the geometry in a collection that lies closest to a given point. The type argument is the kind of geometry held, and must derive from Geometry2d. Every entry is stored together with a snapshot of its extents taken when it was added, and those extents are used to skip candidates that cannot beat the best distance found so far. The snapshot is never refreshed, so a geometry that is moved or changed after it was added will be tested against stale extents and can be missed. Add it again instead of changing it in place. The list is shuffled before the first query after a change, so that the pruning is not defeated by geometry that happens to be added in sorted order.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.Add(`0)
member.summary: Adds a geometry to the collection together with its extents as they are right now. The geometry itself is stored by reference and is not copied. Marks the collection for shuffling before the next query.
member.param: Geometry to add.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.AddRange(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{`0})
member.summary: Adds every geometry in the sequence, each one with its extents as they are right now.
member.param: Geometries to add.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.Remove(`0)
member.summary: Removes a geometry from the collection. The match is made on reference, not on value, so only the very same instance that was added is removed. If the geometry was added more than once only the first entry is removed, and if it is not found at all nothing happens.
member.param: Geometry instance to remove.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.FromPoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Find the geometry that is closest to the given point.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.EnsureShuffled
member.summary: Shuffles the entries into random order if something has been added since the last query, and clears the flag. Random order keeps the extents pruning in FromPoint effective, because geometry added in sorted order would otherwise give the worst case where nothing can be skipped. Does nothing when the collection is already shuffled.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.pairs

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Closest2d`1.shuffle
member.summary: True when something has been added since the last query and the entries need to be shuffled again before the next search.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPair3d
member.summary: Helper methods that find the two points lying closest to each other on a pair of 3d shapes. Every method hands back the answer as a tuple where Item1 lies on the first shape and Item2 on the second, and the two points are always separate objects even when they end up at the same place. The shapes passed in are only read, never changed.

member.summary: Returns the pair which has the points closest to each other.
member.param: Pairs to compare. Passing no pairs at all is allowed.
member.returns: The pair whose two points lie closest to each other, or null when no pairs were given. If several pairs are equally close the first of them is returned.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPair3d.DistTest(System.Tuple{IGS.Genamo.Point3d,IGS.Genamo.Point3d})
member.summary: Measures how far apart the two points of a pair are. Nothing in this file calls it.
member.param: Pair to measure.
member.returns: The distance between the two points of the pair.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPair3d.TriangleSegment(IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d,IGS.Genamo.Line3d)
member.summary: Computes the two points lying closest to each other on a triangle and a line segment. If the segment pierces the triangle, the intersection point is returned twice as two separate points at the same place. Otherwise the best of five candidates is returned: the triangle point closest to each end of the segment, and the closest pair between the segment and each of the three triangle edges. Item1 is on the triangle and Item2 on the segment. Always returns a result and never returns null.
member.param: Triangle to measure against.
Line segment to measure against.
member.returns: A pair where Item1 is the point on the triangle and Item2 the point on the segment.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPair3d.SegmentSegment(IGS.Genamo.Line3d,IGS.Genamo.Line3d)
member.summary: Computes the two points closest to each other on two line segments. Always returns a result, even if the segments are parallel and parametrically overlapping. In that case, a segments endpoint and a point on the other segment is returned as result. In the result, Item1 is on segment 1, and Item2 is on segment2.
member.param: First segment. The returned Item1 lies on this one.
Second segment. The returned Item2 lies on this one.
member.returns: A pair holding the closest point on segment 1 and the closest point on segment 2.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPoints2d
member.summary: Helper methods that compute the closest points between two pieces of 2d geometry. Every method gives the answer back as a Line2d where Start lies on the first shape and End on the second, so the length of that line is the distance between the two shapes. Where the shapes cross, a zero length line at the intersection is returned instead. The shapes passed in are only read and are never changed.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPoints2d.ArcArc(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the closest points between two arc segments. The resulting lines startpoint will be on a1, and its endpoint on a2. 'checkZeroIntersect' should be true if it's possible the segments intersect (ie. check for zero distance) Setting it to false will speed up the computation.
member.param: First arc. The start of the returned line lies on this one. A linear arc is handled as a straight segment.
Second arc. The end of the returned line lies on this one. A linear arc is handled as a straight segment.
True to test for an intersection first and return a zero length line where the arcs cross. When both arcs are linear the test is always made, whatever this is set to.
member.returns: A new line from the closest point on a1 to the closest point on a2. Never null.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPoints2d.ArcSegment(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Line2d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the closest points between an arc segment and a line segment. The resulting lines startpoint will be on arc, and its endpoint on line. 'checkZeroIntersect' should be true if it's possible the segments intersect (ie. check for zero distance) Setting it to false will speed up the computation.
member.param: Arc. The start of the returned line lies on this one. A linear arc is handled as a straight segment.
Line segment. The end of the returned line lies on this one.
True to test for an intersection first and return a zero length line where the arc and the segment cross.
member.returns: A new line from the closest point on the arc to the closest point on the segment. Never null.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPoints2d.SegmentSegment(IGS.Genamo.Line2d,IGS.Genamo.Line2d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes the closest points between two arc segments. The resulting lines startpoint will be on l1, and its endpoint on l2. 'checkZeroIntersect' should be true if it's possible the segments intersect (ie. check for zero distance) Setting it to false will speed up the computation.
member.param: Required.
Required.
Optional. The default value is true. True to test for an intersection first and return a zero length line where the segments cross.
member.returns: A new line from the closest point on l1 to the closest point on l2. Never null.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ClosestPoints2d.PolyPoly(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,IGS.Genamo.Poly2d)
member.summary: Computes the closest points between two polys by testing every edge of the first against every edge of the second, so the cost grows with the product of the two edge counts. Use PolyPoly2 instead when the polys are large. The start of the returned line lies on p1 and the end on p2. Where the polys touch or cross, a zero length line at that point is returned.
member.param: First poly. The start of the returned line lies on this one.
Second poly. The end of the returned line lies on this one.
member.returns: A new line from the closest point on p1 to the closest point on p2, or null if either poly has no edges.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d
member.summary: A conic section given by the six coefficients of the general equation a*x*x + b*x*y + c*y*y + d*x + e*y + f = 0, which covers circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas and the degenerate line cases. The coefficients are public and writable and the Translate method changes them in place, so a conic is not safe to share between callers. Everything else returns a new object or a value. The scale of the coefficients is free, since multiplying all six by the same non zero number describes the same curve.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.CreateFrom5Points(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Creates the conic that passes through five given points, built from the lines joining them. The result is normalised so that the first coefficient that is not zero, taken in the order a, b, c, d, e, becomes exactly 1. Returns a new conic and does not change the points. Five points only determine a conic when they are distinct and no four of them are collinear, so a degenerate set gives either null or a conic that does not pass through them.
member.param: First point.
Second point.
Third point.
Fourth point.
Fifth point.
member.returns: A new conic through the five points, or null when all five leading coefficients come out as exactly zero.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.PolarPoint(IGS.Genamo.Line2d)
member.summary: Returns the pole of line l, or null if not possible (parallel lines etc.)
member.param: Line to take the pole of.
member.returns: The pole of the line. For a degenerate conic the centre is given instead, which is null when a, b and d are all zero. The coordinates are infinite or NaN when the line passes through the centre of the dual conic.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.Center
member.summary: Gets the centre of the conic, computed from the coefficients each time it is read. Returns null when a, b and d are all zero, which is the case of two horizontal lines. A parabola has no centre and gives infinite or NaN coordinates, since the divisor 4*a*c - b*b is then zero.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.PolarLine(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes the polar line of a point with respect to the conic. Since a polar is an infinite line, it is handed back as a segment of arbitrary length that lies on it, so only its direction and position mean anything and its endpoints do not. If the point is the centre of the conic the polar is the line at infinity, and an exception will be thrown.
member.param: Point to take the polar of.
member.returns: A new segment lying on the polar line.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.DualConic
member.summary: Gets the dual conic, that is the adjugate of the coefficient matrix, computed each time it is read. The dual describes the tangent lines of the conic and is used to find the pole of a line. A degenerate conic has no usable dual, since its adjugate is singular as well.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.Determinant
member.summary: Gets the determinant of the three by three coefficient matrix, with the off diagonal terms halved. It is zero exactly for the degenerate conics, and its sign together with the upper two by two determinant tells the conic type apart. Scaling all six coefficients by k scales this by k cubed, so the value on its own says nothing about how close to degenerate a conic is.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.IsDegenerate
member.summary: Gets whether the conic is degenerate, that is whether it falls apart into lines or a point. Tests the determinant against a fixed limit of 1e-100, which is so small that it only catches a determinant that is zero or very nearly so. Since the determinant scales with the cube of the coefficients, the test is not reliable for conics whose coefficients are small.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.Type
member.summary: Gets which kind of conic the coefficients describe, worked out from the determinant, the upper two by two determinant, the trace and the sum of the two remaining two by two determinants. The comparisons are exact, so rounding in the coefficients can move a conic from one kind to another, and a circle is only reported as a circle when a equals c exactly and b is exactly zero. This exactness is also why the result can disagree with IsDegenerate, which uses a tolerance.

member.summary: Computes the centre, rotation and axis lengths of an ellipse. The lengths are measured from the centre, so they are half axes, and the rotation is in radians. If the conic is not an ellipse or a circle, an exception will be thrown.
member.param: Receives the x coordinate of the centre.
Receives the y coordinate of the centre.
Receives the angle in radians from the x axis to the first axis.
Receives the half axis along the phi direction.
Receives the half axis across the phi direction.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.GetHyperbolaParameters(System.Double@,System.Double@,System.Double@,System.Double@,System.Double@)
member.summary: Computes the centre, rotation and axis lengths of a hyperbola. The rotation is in radians and the lengths are measured from the centre. Note that height comes back negative, since the conjugate axis is imaginary and the square root is taken of a negative value and then negated. If the conic is not a hyperbola, an exception will be thrown.
member.param: Receives the x coordinate of the centre.
Receives the y coordinate of the centre.
Receives the angle in radians from the x axis to the transverse axis.
Receives the half axis along the phi direction.
Receives the conjugate half axis, as a negative value.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.GetEquation
member.summary: Gets the six coefficients as an array, in the order a, b, c, d, e, f. The array is newly made on every call, so changing it does not touch the conic.
member.returns: A new array of six coefficients.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Conic2d.Translate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Moves the conic by the given offset, in place. The coefficients a, b and c do not change, only d, e and f. The three updates depend on each other and must stay in the order they are written in, since f is worked out from the already updated d and from the not yet updated e.
member.param: Distance to move along the x axis.
Distance to move along the y axis.

member.summary: Works out which way the turn from p through q to r goes, from the sign of the cross product. The test against zero is exact, so points that are only nearly collinear are still reported as a turn.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ConvexHull2d.GrahamScan(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d})
member.summary: The classical Graham scan, with a cheap pass first that throws away points lying well inside the quadrilateral formed by the leftmost, rightmost, lowest and highest point. That pass uses a fixed margin of 0.1 in model units, so on very small geometry it can drop points that belong on the hull. The returned points are fresh copies, except in the case of fewer than three input points, where the input points themselves are handed back. At least three points are needed for the scan itself, and they must not all be the same point.
member.param: All points the hull should enclose.
member.returns: A new list of new points that in order form the hull. For fewer than three input points, a new list holding the input points themselves.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d
member.summary: Computes the convolution of two polys, which is the Minkowski sum of the first with the second reflected through the origin, so it is the shape used as a no fit polygon when nesting. Both polys are cut into y monotone pieces first, every pair of pieces is convolved on its own, and the pieces come back as a list that the caller still has to union. Only the node points of the polys are used, so a poly with bulges is treated as if the arcs were straight chords. The polys passed in are only read, never changed.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.MinkEdge

member.summary: Direction of the edge in radians, measured from its start point to its end point.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.MinkEdge.DY

member.summary: Checks if the poly changes turning direction across the edge that starts at the given node, by comparing the sign of the turn before it with the sign of the turn after it. Two turns that are both exactly straight count as a change as well, since both signs are then zero. The index wraps, so the poly is treated as closed. Nothing in this file calls it.

member.summary: Reflects a poly through the origin, that is negates both coordinates of every node while keeping the bulges, and marks the result as closed whether or not the original was. Returns a new poly and leaves the original untouched. This is the step that turns a Minkowski sum into the convolution used for no fit polygons.

member.returns: A new closed poly reflected through the origin.

member.summary: Computes the convolution of two polys. The second poly is reflected through the origin first, then both are cut into y monotone pieces and every piece of the first is convolved against every piece of the second. Second poly. It is reflected through the origin before use.

List the pieces of the first poly are appended to.
List the pieces of the second poly are appended to.

member.summary: Builds the merged edge list of two polys, sorted by direction angle. Each entry keeps the step the edge makes and remembers which poly and which index it came from. Only the start and end points of each edge are used, so bulges are ignored and an arc is treated as its chord.
member.param: First poly. Its edges are marked as primary.
Second poly. Its edges are marked as not primary.
member.returns: A new list of edges from both polys, sorted by angle from low to high.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.ConvolveMonotone(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,IGS.Genamo.Poly2d)
member.summary: Convolves two y monotone polys. Slide segments are generated at every convex vertex of each poly, cut against each other at their intersections with a plane sweep, joined into a graph and then walked to pick out the outline. Only the outer contour is returned, so any loops inside it are dropped. If no outgoing edge can be found to start from, an exception will be thrown.
member.param: First monotone poly.
Second monotone poly, already reflected through the origin.
member.returns: A new closed poly holding the outer contour of the convolution.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.IsReflex(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Int32)
member.summary: Checks if a node of a poly is reflex, that is whether the poly turns inward there. A node that lies exactly on the line between its neighbours counts as reflex too, since the test asks only whether the turn is not to the right. The neighbour indices are handed to the poly indexer as they are and rely on it to wrap.
member.param: Poly to look at.
Index of the node to test.
member.returns: True when the node is reflex or exactly straight.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.GetSlideSegs(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.MinkEdge},System.Boolean,IGS.Genamo.PlaneSweep2d,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Line2d},System.Int32@)
member.summary: Generates the slide segments contributed by one of the two polys. At the end vertex of every edge of that poly, the merged edge list is walked forward until the next edge of the same poly is reached, and every edge of the other poly met on the way is copied and placed at that vertex. Reflex vertices are skipped, since nothing slides around them. Each segment is added to both the sweep and the line list, and the running id is stepped on for every one. The walk assumes the closing edge really is in the list, and loops forever if it is not.
member.param: Poly whose vertices the segments are placed at.
The other poly, whose edges are copied.
Merged edge list of both polys, sorted by angle.
Which poly a is, that is true when a is the primary poly.
Plane sweep the segments are added to.
List the segments are appended to, in the same order as the sweep ids.
Running sweep id, stepped on once per segment added.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.PlaneSweepCallback(IGS.Genamo.IExtents2d,IGS.Genamo.IExtents2d,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.PlaneSweepIntersection}@)
member.summary: Callback the plane sweep uses to test one pair of segments. A pair where the end of one is exactly the start of the other is skipped, since sharing an endpoint is not a crossing. A real crossing is added to the result twice, once for each direction, so that the later split step finds it from both segments. Segments that merely lie along each other are not reported.
member.param: First object. Must be a segment.
Second object. Must be a segment.
Sweep id of the first segment.
Sweep id of the second segment.
List the intersections are appended to.
member.returns: Whether an intersection was added.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.CreateTraversal(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Line2d})
member.summary: Builds the graph that is walked to find the outline. Every segment gives two nodes and one edge, nodes lying on the same spot are then merged into one, and finally the edges around every node with more than two of them are sorted by the direction they point in as seen from that node. The merge only looks ahead while the y values are within 1e-9 of each other, which is a much tighter window than the distance the merge itself accepts.
member.param: Segments to build the graph from, already cut at their intersections.
member.returns: A new list of the graph nodes, sorted, with the merged ones removed.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.TracePoly(IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.TravNode},IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.TravNode,IGS.Genamo.Convolve2d.TravEdge)
member.summary: Walks the graph from a start node and start edge to pick out one closed contour. At every node it takes the first outgoing edge that follows the arriving one in the sorted edge order, wrapping around the list, which is what keeps the walk on the outline. The last edge is dropped again before the poly is closed, since it leads back to the node the walk began at. If the arriving edge is not in the node it reaches, or if a node has no outgoing edge to continue with, an exception will be thrown.
member.param: Not used.
Node the walk both begins and ends at.
Edge to leave the start node along.
member.returns: A new closed poly holding the contour that was walked.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d
member.summary: Cuts a region into simpler pieces, either y monotone polys or triangles. The region is first copied into a doubly connected edge list, where every contour edge becomes a pair of half edges pointing opposite ways, then the classic sweep adds diagonals from split and merge vertices, and finally the faces of that structure are read back out as polys. Only the node points of the input are used, so a region with bulges is treated as if every arc were its chord, and the points are rounded to RoundingAccuracy on the way in. The region passed in is only read, never changed. If the input is self intersecting or otherwise inconsistent, an exception will be thrown.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.RoundingAccuracy
member.summary: Grid the input coordinates are snapped to before anything else happens, which is what makes points that are almost equal come out exactly equal. Must be greater than zero, since the number of decimals is taken from its logarithm.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.InsertionSort(IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriEdge,IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriEdge)
member.summary: Inserts an edge into the circular list of edges around a node, keeping the list sorted by angle from low to high, and with the longer edge first where two share an angle. The list is linked in place through the Next and Prev fields of the edges, so nothing is copied. Angles are compared exactly.
member.param: Head of the circular list, or null when the list is still empty.
Edge to insert.
member.returns: The head of the list afterwards, which is the inserted edge when it sorted first.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.InsertEdge(IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriNode,IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriNode,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriEdge})
member.summary: Adds an edge between two nodes as a pair of half edges pointing opposite ways, appends both to the edge list and links each into the circular edge list of the node it leaves. A contour edge also sets the next and previous node links and marks only the forward half as being on the material side, while a diagonal marks both halves as material so that the faces on either side of it are kept.
member.param: Node the forward half edge leaves from.
Node the forward half edge arrives at.
True for a diagonal added by the sweep, false for an edge of the original contour.
List both half edges are appended to.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.CollectFaces(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriNode}},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriNode},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriEdge})
member.summary: Walks the edge structure and reads out every face, by following each edge to the previous edge around its twin until the walk comes back to where it started. A face is kept only when every one of its edges is on the material side, which is what throws away the faces that lie in holes or outside the outline. Clears the visited flag on all edges first, so it can be run more than once.
member.param: List each face is appended to, as the list of nodes around it.
Not used.
All half edges of the structure.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.PolyToDCEL(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriEdge},System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriNode},System.Int32)
member.summary: Copies one poly into the edge structure. Every point is first rounded to RoundingAccuracy, then points that land closer together than Calc.Epsilon are dropped, and the last point is dropped as well when it has collapsed onto the first. A poly left with fewer than three points is skipped altogether and nothing is added. Only node points are used, so bulges are ignored and an arc is treated as its chord. Every node remembers which contour and which index it came from, so the result can be reported back against the original data.
member.param: Poly to copy in.
List the half edges are appended to.
List the nodes that survived are appended to.
Number stored on every node to say which poly it came from.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.ClassifyNodes(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Decompose2d.TriNode})
member.summary: Works out what kind of vertex each node is, which is what decides where the sweep has to add a diagonal. A node is a start or an end where the contour turns around and the inside is on the expected side, a split or a merge where it turns around the other way, and regular otherwise. The decision uses the y values of the two neighbours together with the sign of the perpendicular dot product, and the comparisons are exact, so the classification of nodes that share a y value depends on their exact coordinates. Afterwards each contour is walked once more to mark every node as lying on the left or the right side. Both passes write to the nodes in place.
member.param: Nodes to classify. Every one must already have its next and previous node set.

member.param: Active edge list to remove from.
Node to remove.
member.returns: True when the node was found and removed, false when it was not in the list.

member.summary: Finds the entry of the active edge list whose edge is the nearest one to the left of a node, by working out where each edge crosses the height of that node and keeping the largest crossing that is still not to the right of it. The whole list is scanned every time, so this is linear in the number of active edges rather than the logarithmic lookup the algorithm assumes.
member.param: Active edge list to search.
Node to search to the left of.
member.returns: The node owning the nearest edge to the left, or null when no edge lies to the left.

member.summary: Orders two nodes the way the sweep needs them, that is from the top down: higher y first, then lower x first, and finally by vertex type in the order the type list is written in, so that nodes sharing a point are still handled in a fixed order.
