member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Dijkstra
member.summary: A weighted directed graph together with a shortest path search over it. Nodes are added first, then linked with Connect, and FindShortestPath fills in the distance and the previous node on every node it reaches, so the path is read back by walking the previous chain from the end node. The search writes into the node objects themselves, so the same nodes cannot be used by two searches at once, and they have to be added again before a second run.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Dijkstra.Q
member.summary: The graph itself: for every node that has been added, the nodes it links to and what each link costs. A node with no outgoing links still has an entry, holding an empty list.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Dijkstra.Add(IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode)
member.summary: Adds a node to the dijkstra graph, returning a reference to itself.
member.param: Node to add. Its distance, previous node and visited flag are all reset, and any links it already had in this graph are thrown away.
member.returns: The very node that was passed in, so a call can be chained.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Dijkstra.Connect(IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode,IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode,System.Double)
member.summary: Adds a one way link from one node to another. Call it twice, once each way, for a link that can be walked in both directions. The source node must already have been added, otherwise an exception will be thrown; the target is not checked here, and a target that was never added makes the search fail later instead.
member.param: Node the link starts at. Must already be in the graph.
Node the link ends at.
Weight of the link.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Dijkstra.FindShortestPath(IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode,IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode)
member.summary: Runs the search out from the start node, filling in the distance and the previous node on every node it reaches. Nothing is returned; the caller reads the path by walking the previous chain back from the node it is interested in, and a node whose distance is still double.MaxValue was never reached. Every node in the graph has to have been added, otherwise an exception will be thrown when the search steps onto it. The end node is not looked at, so the search always runs over the whole graph. Note that a node is put back on the queue after every relaxation attempt whether or not it improved, so a graph with a cycle in it keeps the loop going forever.
member.param: Node to search out from. Its distance is set to zero.
Not used.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Dijkstra.ExtractMinNode(IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode@,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Tuple{IGS.Genamo.DijkstraNode,System.Double}}@)
member.summary: Takes the unvisited node with the smallest distance out of the graph and hands back its neighbours as well, by scanning every entry each time. It removes the node from the graph as it goes, so the graph is emptied as the search runs. Nothing calls it any more, since the search now uses a priority queue.
member.param: Receives the node with the smallest distance, or null when none was found.
Receives the links leading out of that node, or null when none was found.
member.returns: True when a node was found and removed, false when the graph was already empty.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1
member.summary: A binary min heap of items with a weight each, used by the shortest path search to pick the cheapest node to work on next. The type argument is whatever is being queued. The items and their weights are held in two arrays that grow by doubling, and the same item can be queued more than once, since there is no way to change the weight of an item already in the queue.

member.summary: The queued items, in heap order. Only the first Count entries mean anything.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1._weights
member.summary: Weight of each queued item, kept in step with the item array.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1._count

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1.IsEmpty

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1.#ctor

member.summary: Compares the weights of two queued items by their place in the arrays.

Place of the second item.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1.reheapifyUp(System.Int32)
member.summary: Moves a newly added item up the heap until its parent weighs no more than it does, which is what restores the heap after an item is put at the end.
member.param: Place of the item to move up.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PriorityQueue`1.reheapifyDown(System.Int32)
member.summary: Moves an item down the heap until both its children weigh at least as much as it does, which is what restores the heap after the smallest item is taken off the top. The case of a node with only one child is handled on its own.
member.param: Place of the item to move down.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d
member.summary: The ellipse can represent either a full ellipse or an elliptical arc. The ellipse can be tilted in world space, using the angle of the major axis. Degenerate ellipses (one of the axis is zero length) is not supported and will most likely produce odd results and exceptions. The elliptical arc is always seen as counter clockwise and the major axis is always the longest axis of the ellipse. Constuctors will swap axes and angles so that this conditions are fullfilled. A word about our definition of elliptical parameters: an elliptical parameter is in range 0-2pi, where parameter 0 is the right quadrant point of the ellipse in the ellipses local coordinate system. When the ellipse is an arc, the paramteric range of this arc is a sub part of this parametric range, which means an arc can for example have startparameter=0.3 endparameter=0.8.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.Flatten(System.Double)
member.summary: Approximates the ellipse or elliptical arc with a polyline of straight segments, by splitting each chord at the middle until the curve is close enough to it. A full ellipse comes back as a closed poly, an arc as an open one. Returns a new poly and leaves this object untouched. Note that the test against the tolerance uses a signed distance, so a chord whose midpoint falls on one particular side is accepted however far from the curve it lies.
member.param: Largest distance the polyline may stray from the curve, in model units.
member.returns: A new poly following the ellipse, closed when this is a full ellipse.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.ClosestPoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes the point on the ellipse or elliptical arc lying closest to another point, by taking the nearest of the perpendicular foot points and, for an arc, also weighing the two end points. Note that when a later foot point turns out to be nearer than the one held so far, the point passed in is stored instead of that foot point, so the result can be the argument itself rather than a point on the curve.
member.param: Point to be as close as possible to.
member.returns: The closest point found. Not always a point on the ellipse, see above.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.ArcFit(System.Int32)
member.summary: Approximates the ellipse with a fixed number of circular arcs, placed by curvature so the fit is best where the curve bends most. The arcs are built for one quadrant and mirrored into the other three, so the count is rounded up to a multiple of four and is never below two. An elliptical arc is cut out of the full approximation afterwards. Returns a new poly of arc segments and leaves this object untouched.
member.param: Number of arcs to build the quadrant from. Values below two are raised to two.
member.returns: A new poly of circular arcs following the ellipse, closed when this is a full ellipse.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.ArcFit(System.Double)
member.summary: Approximates the ellipse with circular arcs, splitting each arc in two until it lies within the given tolerance of the true curve. A full ellipse is built from two half arcs using symmetry, an arc from a single starting arc. Returns a new poly of arc segments and leaves this object untouched.
member.param: Largest distance the arcs may stray from the curve, in model units.
member.returns: A new poly of circular arcs following the ellipse.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.ToConic
member.summary: Converts the ellipse to the general conic that describes it. The conic covers the full ellipse, so the start and end parameters of an arc are lost. Returns a new conic and leaves this object untouched.
member.returns: A new conic with the same coefficients as GetEquation gives.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.DualConic(IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d)
member.summary: Computes the dual conic of this ellipse with respect to another one, which is the curve through the poles that the tangents of this ellipse have in the other. Five points are sampled along this ellipse, each is turned into a tangent line, each line is mapped to its pole in the other ellipse, and a conic is fitted through the five poles. The result is expected to be a hyperbola but is not checked. Returns null when no conic can be fitted through the five poles.
member.param: Ellipse the tangent lines are mapped to poles in.
member.returns: A new conic through the five poles, or null when none could be fitted.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.Contains(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Checks if a point lies inside the ellipse, using the rule that the two distances to the foci add up to no more than the major axis. The test is made against the filled full ellipse, so the start and end parameters of an arc are ignored and a point exactly on the circumference counts as inside. The comparison is exact, with no tolerance.
member.param: Point to test.
member.returns: True when the point is inside or exactly on the full ellipse.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d.CommonTangents(IGS.Genamo.Ellipse2d)
member.summary: Computes the lines that touch both this ellipse and another one. The points of tangency are found by intersecting each ellipse with the dual conic of the other, and a pair of them is kept when the line between them runs along the tangent of both curves, to within the angle tolerance of Calc.AngleEquals. Returns a new array, which is empty when no pair passes the test, and leaves both ellipses untouched.
member.param: The other ellipse.
member.returns: A new array of the common tangent lines, empty when none were found.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Extents2d.Split(IGS.Genamo.Extents2d)
member.summary: Splits this extent into the strips that lie outside another one, giving up to four boxes: one on each side of the other box that this extent reaches past. The strips are not cut against each other, so the left and right ones run the full height while the bottom and top ones run the full width, and the four corner areas are therefore covered twice. Note also that an extent which does not overlap the other one at all gives an empty list rather than a copy of itself. Returns new extents and leaves both this one and the argument untouched.
member.param: Box to cut away from this one.
member.returns: A new list of up to four new extents, empty when the two boxes do not overlap.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster
member.summary: Groups points by the FLAME method, which looks only at how the points sit relative to their nearest neighbours rather than at absolute positions. Points are added first, then Calculate builds each point's neighbour list, works out its density and marks it as a cluster seed, an outlier or an ordinary point. Note that the last step of the method, the one that spreads memberships out from the seeds and actually forms the clusters, is commented out at the bottom of this file, so as it stands the class classifies points but does not group them.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.Points
member.summary: Every point added so far, in the order they were added. Public, so a caller reads the type and the density of each point straight from here after Calculate.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.K
member.summary: How many nearest neighbours each point keeps. Overwritten by the value handed to Calculate, so the twenty here only holds until then.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.#ctor
member.summary: Creates a new empty clustering with no points in it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.Add(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Adds a point to the clustering. The point is wrapped and held by reference rather than copied. Adding points after Calculate has run does not update anything until it is run again.
member.param: Point to add.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.Calculate(System.Int32)
member.summary: Builds the neighbour lists and classifies every point as a seed, an outlier or ordinary, writing the result into the points themselves. The outlier threshold is fixed here at two tenths of a standard deviation above the mean density. Nothing is reset first, so running it a second time starts from the types the first run left behind. With fewer than two points, an exception will be thrown.
member.param: How many nearest neighbours each point should keep.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.PreparePoints
member.summary: Fills in the nearest neighbour list of every point, by measuring every pair of points once and offering each to the other. The cost grows with the square of the number of points, and each offer re-sorts a neighbour list, so this is the expensive step.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.FlameCluster.DefineSupports(System.Double)
member.summary: Works out the density of every point from its neighbour distances, then marks the points that are denser than all their neighbours as seeds and the thin ones below the threshold as outliers. The threshold is the mean density plus the given factor times the standard deviation. Note that the test which pushes a point away from being a seed reads the type of its neighbours while those types are still being decided in the same pass, so the outcome depends on the order the points happen to be in and on anything left over from an earlier run. If any point has no neighbours, an exception will be thrown.
member.param: How many standard deviations above the mean density the outlier limit sits. The value is overwritten inside the method with the limit itself.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.GeometricClustering
member.summary:
HDBSCAN-based spatial clustering for 2D shapes.
Given a set of Poly2d shapes, identifies groups of shapes that are spatially close together, without requiring the number of clusters to be specified in advance. Handles clusters of varying density.
Algorithm: Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering (HDBSCAN) 1. Compute mutual reachability distances between shape centroids 2. Build minimum spanning tree (Prim's algorithm) 3. Build single-linkage dendrogram 4. Condense dendrogram (collapse spurious splits) 5. Extract optimal flat clustering via excess-of-mass 6. Assign noise points to nearest cluster
Time complexity: O(n²) where n is the number of shapes. Suitable for up to ~5000 shapes.

member.param: The shapes to cluster.
Minimum number of shapes to form a cluster. Use -1 for automatic estimation. Larger values produce fewer, bigger clusters.
Controls density estimation. Lower values detect sparser clusters and produce less noise. Use -1 for automatic.
member.returns: A list of shape clusters, sorted by Id.

member.summary:
Condenses the dendrogram and extracts optimal clusters using HDBSCAN's excess-of-mass method.
Condensation: Walk the dendrogram top-down. At each split, if one side has fewer than minClusterSize points, those points "fall out" as noise and the cluster continues. Only splits where both sides are large enough create new child clusters.
Extraction: For each condensed cluster, compute stability = how long points stay in the cluster. Select the set of non-overlapping clusters that maximizes total stability.
member.param: First child of each internal dendrogram node.
Second child of each internal dendrogram node.
Weight at which each internal node was formed.
Number of points under each internal node.
Number of points.
Fewest points a split has to leave on both sides for it to count as a real split rather than points falling out as noise.
member.returns: A new array with one label per point. A point that ended up outside every chosen cluster gets a negative label.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1
member.summary: A fixed size grid that speeds up finding which objects lie near a given box. The area is split into a fixed number of cells once at construction, and every object added is registered in each cell its extents reach into, together with a snapshot of those extents. The type argument is whatever is being stored and has to expose its extents. The extents are read once when an object is added, so moving an object afterwards leaves it filed in the wrong cells.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.grid
member.summary: The cells, each holding the objects registered in it together with the extents they had when they were added. A cell stays null until something is put in it.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.all
member.summary: Every object added so far, in the order they were added.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.box
member.summary: The area the grid covers, grown slightly beyond the box handed to the constructor so that objects sitting exactly on the edge still land inside.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.xcnt
member.summary: Number of columns in the grid.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.ycnt
member.summary: Number of rows in the grid.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.Extents
member.summary: Gets a reference to the area the grid covers. This is the grown box, not the one that was handed to the constructor, and changing it changes the grid.

The area is copied and then grown by a thousandth so that objects on the edge still fall inside. The counts have to be at least one, and the area needs a real width and height, since every lookup divides by them.

Number of columns.
Number of rows.

member.summary: Registers an object in every cell its extents reach into, and remembers those extents as they are right now. An object that is moved afterwards stays filed under the old extents and will be found in the wrong place. Adding the same object twice files it twice.

member.returns: A new list of the objects found, empty when the grid has no cells or nothing overlaps.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGrid2d`1.CollectWithExtents(IGS.Genamo.Extents2d)

member.returns: A new list of the objects found, each paired with the extents it was filed under.

member.summary: Gets every object that has been added, in the order they were added. This hands back the grid's own list rather than a copy, so changing it changes what the grid thinks it holds.
member.returns: The internal list of added objects.

Unlike GeometryGrid2d an arc is only registered in a cell when it really comes close to that cell's centre, not merely when its extents overlap, so the grid holds fewer entries. The extents of an arc are read once when it is added.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.GeometryGridArc2d.Add(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d)
member.summary: Registers an arc in the cells it comes close to. The cells its extents cover are visited, and the arc is only filed in a cell when the true distance from the arc to that cell's centre is within the cell radius, so a long thin arc across a cell corner is skipped. The extents are remembered as they are right now, so an arc that is changed afterwards is filed wrongly.
member.param: Arc to register. Stored by reference and not copied.

member.summary: Removes an arc from the grid and from the list of added arcs. The cells are found from the arc's extents as they are now, so an arc that has been changed since it was added may not be removed from every cell it sits in. Entries are matched with the equality operator, so which arcs are removed depends on how Arc2d defines equality.
member.param: Arc to remove.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.SegmentGrid
member.summary: A fixed size grid of line segments, built for walking a line or a ray across the grid and picking up the segments it may cross. member.summary: Walks a line across the grid and hands the callback every segment it meets on the way, together with the cell it was found in. A segment stored in several cells is only offered once. Note that a callback returning true only stops the rest of the current cell, not the walk, and that a segment refused this way is not marked as seen and can be offered again from a later cell.

Called for each segment met, with the segment and its cell. Return true to skip the rest of that cell.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SegmentGrid.Traverse(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,System.Func{IGS.Genamo.Line2d,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean})
member.summary: Walks a ray from a point in a given direction across the grid and hands the callback every segment it meets. The ray is cut to the length of the grid diagonal, so a direction that leads away from the grid finds nothing. Note that the direction vector is normalised in place, so the one handed in is changed.
member.param: Point the ray starts at.
Direction of the ray. Normalised in place.
Called for each segment met, with the segment and its cell. Return true to skip the rest of that cell.

member.summary: Collects every segment lying in a cell that a line passes through. This is a rough pass: a segment is returned because it shares a cell with the line, not because the two really cross, so the caller still has to test them. Returns a new list with each segment only once.

member.returns: A new list of the segments sharing a cell with the line.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SegmentGrid.Traverse(IGS.Genamo.Line2d,System.Action{System.Int32,System.Int32})
member.summary: Walks the cells that a line passes through and calls back once for each, stepping from cell to cell along the line rather than filling in its whole bounding box. The line is first clipped to the grid, and nothing happens at all when it falls completely outside. The cell indices handed to the callback are not range checked.
member.param: Line to walk along.
Called once per cell, with the column and the row.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.IniFile
member.summary: Reads and writes a simple ini file, holding the whole file in memory as sections of key and value pairs. The file is read once when the object is created and only written back when something has changed, either through UpdateFile or when the object is disposed. Note that a rewrite loses anything the reader ignored, so comment lines in the original file are dropped. Values are escaped on the way in and unescaped on the way out, so a value may hold newlines and other control characters.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IniFile.disposed

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.InsidePoly2d.IPSeg.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Orders two entries by the bottom of their extents, so the list can be walked from the lowest upwards. Note that it never gives back zero: two entries whose extents start at the same height each report themselves as the greater one, which is not a consistent ordering and can make the sort throw. The two circles are ordered internally so the larger one is first, and the point is placed on the larger circle along the line joining the centres. Circles that miss each other by less than the tolerance, either by standing apart or by one lying inside the other, are treated as touching and give back a single point. Circles that coincide give nothing, since there is no finite answer. Note that the two-point branch only reports a single intersection when the centre distance equals the sum of the radii exactly, which floating point arithmetic almost never produces, so near tangency normally comes back as two points that lie very close together.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Intersect2d.ConicConic(IGS.Genamo.Conic2d,IGS.Genamo.Conic2d)
member.summary: Computes the points where two conics cross. Both conics are copied and shifted so that the midpoint of their centres sits at origin, which keeps the coefficients small, and the results are shifted back before being returned. The quartic resultant is solved once for the y values and once, with the coefficients swapped, for the x values, and each real y is then paired with whichever unused real x gives the smallest error in the two conic equations. That pairing is accepted whatever the error is, so a point can come back that does not actually lie on either conic when the two root lists do not match up.
member.param: The first conic to intersect. Not modified; a copy is worked on.
The second conic to intersect. Not modified; a copy is worked on.
member.returns: A new list of the crossing points, at most four, in the original coordinate system. Empty when no real pair was found.

member.summary: Callback handed to the plane sweep when a poly is intersected with itself. It sorts the pair so the lower edge index comes first, works out whether the two edges are neighbours in the poly, and appends the crossings it finds. Crossings that fall within 1e-5 of any of the four end points are left out, and touching end points are then added back under the tighter epsilon tolerance, skipping the pairs where the two edges are neighbours and so share a point anyway. Reads the edge count and the closed flag from the static fields set by PolySelfIntersect.

The second arc of the pair. Must really be an Arc2d, since it is cast without a check.

member.summary: This static class contains various intersection algorithms for 3d objects: lines and segments against planes, triangles, quads, spheres, discs, cylinders and cones, and planes and quads against each other. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Intersect3d.LineSphereParametric(IGS.Genamo.Line3d,IGS.Genamo.Point3d,System.Double,System.Double@)
member.summary: Computes where a ray first meets a sphere. The ray starts at the line's start point and runs in the direction of its end point, and only the near of the two crossings is reported. Note that despite the name the value handed back is a distance in model units and not a parameter from zero to one along the line, since the direction is normalised and the line length is never used. A start point inside the sphere gives a negative distance, and the far side of the sphere is never reported.

Center of the sphere.
Radius of the sphere.
Set to the distance from the start point to the near crossing, or to zero when there is none. Negative when the start point lies inside the sphere.
member.returns: true when the ray meets the sphere, false when it misses it or points away from it.

member.summary: Computes the segment along which two triangles cut each other. Each edge of one triangle is tested against the other triangle and the two points furthest apart are joined. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Intersect3d.TriangleTriangle(IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d,IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d)
member.summary: Checks whether two triangles cut each other, without working out where. Each triangle's corners are first measured against the other's plane and the pair is dropped when they all fall on one side; a corner lying exactly in the plane counts as the same side, so triangles that only touch are reported as not meeting. What survives is then checked edge by edge. As the note in the body says, a crossing that runs exactly along a triangle boundary can be missed.
member.param: The first triangle to test.
The second triangle to test.
member.returns: true when the triangles cut each other, otherwise false. Also false when either normal works out as not a number, which happens for a degenerate triangle.

member.summary: Computes where a line segment passes through a triangle. The triangle is taken as two sided: the winding is flipped internally when the segment comes at it from behind. A segment lying in the plane of the triangle is rejected. Note that the output point is set to a default point at origin rather than to null when nothing is found, so callers must go by the return value.
member.param: The triangle to intersect.
The segment to intersect. Only the part between its two end points counts.
Set to a new point where the segment pierces the triangle, or to a default point at origin when there is none.

member.summary: Computes where an infinite line passes through a triangle and hands back the parameter along the line. This is the same test as TriangleSegment without the check that keeps the hit between the two end points, so a crossing well beyond either end is still reported. The triangle is taken as two sided and a line lying in its plane is rejected. Note that the parameter is left holding an unscaled working value rather than being cleared when the corner tests fail, so it must only be read after a true result.

member.summary: Computes the segment along which two quads cut each other. Every edge of each quad is tested against the other quad and the two points furthest apart are joined, so at least two crossing points are needed. member.summary: Computes the segment along which a plane cuts a triangle. Each of the three edges is crossed with the plane and the two points furthest apart are joined. member.summary: Computes where a ray first meets a rounded cone, that is the body swept by a sphere whose centre runs from one point to the other while its radius changes. The side of the cone is tried first and the two end spheres after it. The value handed back is a parameter along the line, zero at the start point and one at the end point, but it is not held to that range, so a hit behind the start or beyond the end still comes back and the caller has to check. Note that when only the second end sphere is hit, the running best is still at its no-hit starting value of minus one and the comparison drops the hit; note as well that the miss reported from the end sphere step is minus one divided by the line length rather than a plain minus one.

Centre of the sphere at the first end.
Centre of the sphere at the other end.
Radius at the first end.
Radius at the other end.
member.returns: The parameter along the line where the ray meets the cone, or a negative value when it misses. The miss value is minus one from the side test and minus one over the line length from the end sphere test.

Radius at the other end.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1
member.summary: A centred interval tree over one dimensional ranges, holding an object of the caller's type with each range. Ranges are added one at a time and the tree is built the first time a lookup is made, so adding is cheap but adding and looking up in turn rebuilds the whole tree every time. The class enumerates the stored objects in the order they were added, not in range order.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITInterval`1
member.summary: One stored range together with the object it belongs to. The type of the object is declared here on its own, so it is not tied to the type of the tree holding it, although in practice the two are always the same.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITInterval`1.min
member.summary: Low end of the range. Public, so it can be changed from outside, but doing so leaves mid out of step since mid is only worked out when the range is created or translated.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITInterval`1.max
member.summary: High end of the range. Public, so it can be changed from outside, but doing so leaves mid out of step since mid is only worked out when the range is created or translated.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITInterval`1.mid
member.summary: Midpoint of the range, worked out once when the range is created and shifted again by Translate. It is what the ranges are sorted by while the tree is built.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITInterval`1.obj
member.summary: The object this range stands for. Held by reference, so it is not copied on the way in.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITInterval`1.#ctor(`1,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Creates a new range holding an object, and works out the midpoint from the two ends. The two ends are taken as given, so passing them the wrong way round is not caught.
member.param: Object to hold. Kept by reference.
Low end of the range.
High end of the range.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITNode`1
member.summary: One node of the tree. It holds the ranges that straddle its split value, and hands the ranges lying wholly below or wholly above it to its two children. The type of the objects is declared here on its own, in the same way as on the range class.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITNode`1.mid
member.summary: Split value of this node, the median of the midpoints of the ranges it was built from.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITNode`1.left
member.summary: The ranges straddling the split value, sorted by their low end from the smallest upwards. Used when the value looked for lies at or below the split, so the walk can stop as soon as a range starts above it.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITNode`1.right
member.summary: The same ranges as in left, sorted by their high end from the largest downwards. Used when the value looked for lies above the split, so the walk can stop as soon as a range ends below it. The two lists hold the same range objects, not copies.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITNode`1.lc
member.summary: Child node holding the ranges that lie wholly below the split value. Null when there are none.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ITNode`1.rc
member.summary: Child node holding the ranges that lie wholly above the split value. Null when there are none.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.root
member.summary: Root of the built tree, or null when the tree has not been built yet or was thrown away because a range was added. A lookup builds it again when it finds it null.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.intervals
member.summary: Every range added so far. Public, and reordered by Construct, which sorts it by midpoint, so after the first lookup its order no longer matches the order things were added in.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.objects
member.summary: Every object added so far, in the order they were added. This list is never reordered, so it stops lining up index for index with the intervals list once the tree has been built. It is what the enumerator walks.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.Add(`0,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Adds a range and the object belonging to it. The built tree is thrown away, so the next lookup builds it again from scratch; adding and looking up in turn is therefore expensive.

member.summary: Empties the tree of every range and object and throws the built tree away, leaving it as if nothing had been added.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.Construct
member.summary: Builds the tree from the ranges added so far. It is called on its own by the lookups when the tree is missing, so it rarely needs calling from outside. Note that it sorts the public intervals list by midpoint, which leaves that list in a different order from the objects list.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.ConstructRecursive(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree{`0}.ITInterval{`0}})
member.summary: Builds one node and the tree below it. The node's split value is the median of the midpoints; ranges ending below it go to the left child, ranges starting above it go to the right child, and the rest are kept on the node itself in two orders. The way the median is chosen always leaves at least one range on the node, so the recursion always ends.
member.param: Ranges to build this part of the tree from, already sorted by midpoint.
member.returns: The new node, or null when the list is empty.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree`1.Median(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.IntervalTree{`0}.ITInterval{`0}})
member.summary: Picks the split value from a list of ranges already sorted by midpoint. Note that the two branches look to be the wrong way round: an even count takes a single midpoint while an odd count averages the two around the middle, which is the opposite of the usual reading of a median. The value is still a workable split, so the tree is correct either way.
member.param: Ranges to take the split value from, sorted by midpoint. Must not be empty.
member.returns: The split value for a node built from these ranges.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.FastInside

The edges are held twice in interval trees, once by the span they cover in y and once by the span they cover in x, so a test only has to look at the edges that can reach the point's row or column. Note that every edge is taken as a straight line between two poly points, so an arc is treated as its chord.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinNode.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Orders two nodes by y first and then by x, so that nodes sitting on exactly the same spot end up next to each other when the list is sorted. The two coordinates are compared exactly, with no tolerance, so endpoints that are merely close are not treated as equal here; those are brought together later through the join distance instead. It also assumes the object really is a node, so anything else gives a null reference.
member.param: Node to compare with. Must be a node of this same type.
member.returns: Minus one when this node comes first, one when it comes after, and zero when the two sit on exactly the same spot.

member.summary: One piece of geometry waiting to be joined, together with the node at each of its two ends and a flag saying whether the walk has already taken it.

member.summary: Creates a new edge around a poly. The poly is held by reference and not copied, so reversing the edge during the join reverses the caller's poly as well.

member.summary: The geometry of this edge. Reversed in place while the chain is being built, so it does not necessarily still run the way it did when it was added.

member.summary: The largest gap between two endpoints that is still joined, as handed to Compute. Zero switches the gap closing off altogether and only endpoints meeting exactly are joined.

member.summary: The join distance squared, so that gaps can be measured without taking a square root. Only used when deciding whether a finished chain closes back on itself.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.Compute(System.Double)
member.summary: Joins the geometry added with the Add functions. Geometry will be joined if the endpoints are within _joindist.
member.param: The maximum distance between endpoints. If exact join is wanted set this to Calc.Epsilon to avoid double precision erros.
member.returns: A new Region2d with the joined geometry.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.Join(IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinEdge)
member.summary: Follows a chain of edges out from one edge and adds what it finds to the result. A piece that is already a closed poly is copied straight into the result. Otherwise edges are taken one after another, each reversed if need be so that it runs on from the one before, until nothing more can be followed; when the far end runs out, the chain is turned round and the search carries on from what was its start. Coming back to a node the walk has already been through closes a loop, which is unwound into the result there and then before the walk carries on with whatever is left.
member.param: Edge to start the chain from. It must already be flagged as used.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.AddVisitedEdges(IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinEdge})
member.summary: Turns a chain of edges into a single poly and empties the chain as it goes. The edges are taken off the end of the chain and each is reversed as it is added, so the poly runs the opposite way round from the way the chain was built. When the two ends of the finished poly are no further apart than the join distance, the last point is dropped and the poly is marked closed.
member.param: Chain of edges to turn into a poly. Emptied by this method, which is what tells the caller how much is left.
member.returns: A new poly running along the chain, closed when its two ends met.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.AddToPoly(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinEdge)
member.summary: Appends one edge to the poly being built, working in place on that poly. The edge's own poly is copied first and the copy is the one reversed, so the edge itself is left as it was; the reversal is what makes the pieces line up, since the chain is walked from its last edge backwards.
member.param: Poly being built. Added to in place.
Edge to append.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.SelectNext(IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinEdge,IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinNode)
member.summary: Picks the next edge to follow on from a node. The unused edges meeting the node exactly are tried first. When none is left, and only where the node is a loose end with no more than one edge on it, the kd tree is asked for nodes nearby and their unused edges are tried instead. Note that the kd tree is asked for everything in a square box reaching the join distance in each direction and the real distance is never measured afterwards, so a gap lying diagonally can be closed even when it is up to about forty per cent wider than the join distance asked for.
member.param: Edge the chain is coming in on.
Node the chain has reached, and where the next edge must start.
member.returns: The edge to follow, or null when nothing is left to follow.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.SelectNext(IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinEdge,IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinNode,IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.Join2d.JoinEdge})
member.summary: Picks the best of a set of candidate edges to follow on from a node. The direction the chain is travelling in as it arrives is worked out from the tangent of the current edge at that end, and each candidate is measured by how far its own tangent lies from that direction going clockwise. The one turning the least clockwise wins, which is the rule that keeps the walk hugging one side of the geometry and so traces out whole loops rather than cutting across them.
member.param: Edge the chain is coming in on.
Node the chain has reached. Which end of the incoming edge this is decides which of its two tangents is used.
Candidate edges to choose between. All of them are considered, whether or not they really touch the node.
member.returns: The candidate turning least clockwise, or null when the list is empty.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Join2d.MergeNodes
member.summary: Folds together the endpoints that sit on exactly the same spot, so that each remaining node carries every edge meeting there. The list is sorted first, which brings equal nodes next to each other, and each run of them is then collapsed onto the first, with the edges pointed at the one that is kept. Coordinates are compared exactly here, so endpoints that are merely close are left alone and are only brought together later through the join distance.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.KDTree2d`1
member.summary: The KDTree2d class is a 2d variant of a general KD tree. This data structure is used too rapidly find points in the plane who resides in a given bounding box.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.KDTree2d`1.root
member.summary: Root of the tree, or null while the tree is empty. Objects are only ever added, so it is only set back to null by Clear.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.KDTree2d`1.size
member.summary: Number of objects added so far. Kept up to date only by the insert, so it goes out of step with the tree if the public node fields are used to change the shape of it from outside.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.KDTree2d`1.RecursiveInsert(`0@,IGS.Genamo.KDNode2d{`0}@,System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds one object below a node, going down the tree until an empty place is found and hanging the new node there. The two coordinates are used in turn, x at even levels and y at odd ones, and an object whose coordinate on the level is equal to the node's goes to the right. Nothing is done to keep the tree balanced, so objects handed in already sorted build a tree that is little more than a chain, which makes both adding and searching slow and can run the stack out on a large set.
member.param: Object to add. Passed by reference only to save copying; it is not changed.
The place in the tree to add below. Set to the new node when it is null, so the caller's field or child pointer is filled in by this call.
Which coordinate to split on: zero for x, one for y. It alternates on the way down.
member.returns: The node that was reached or created, which is the same value written back through the node parameter.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.KDTree2d`1.RecursiveGetRange(System.Double@,System.Double@,System.Double@,System.Double@,IGS.Genamo.KDNode2d{`0}@,System.Collections.Generic.List{`0}@,System.Int32)
member.summary: Gathers the objects inside a box from one node and the tree below it. The node's own object is taken when it lies in the box, edges counting as inside, and a child is only entered when the box reaches past the node on that child's side, which is what keeps whole branches from being looked at. The box must already be the right way round, with the first corner below the second.
member.param: Left edge of the box.
Bottom edge of the box.
Right edge of the box.
Top edge of the box.
Node to search from. Nothing is done when it is null.
List that the objects found are appended to.
Which coordinate this node splits on: zero for x, one for y.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1
member.summary: Walks a LinkList from its first node to its last. It is the plain non-generic enumerator, so a foreach over a list yields object rather than the stored type. It does not notice the list being changed while it is walking, and once it has run off the end it starts again from the beginning if it is asked for another step.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1.pos
member.summary: Node the walk currently stands on, or null before the first step and after the last one.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1.lst
member.summary: The list being walked. Only its first node is ever read, so the walk carries on along whatever links the nodes hold even after the list has let go of them.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1.#ctor(IGS.Genamo.LinkList{`0})
member.summary: Creates a new enumerator standing before the first node of a list. A step has to be taken before anything can be read.
member.param: List to walk. Kept by reference.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1.Reset
member.summary: Puts the walk back before the first node, so that the next step lands on the list's first node as it stands at that moment.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1.Current
member.summary: Gets the object on the node the walk stands on. Reading it before the first step, or after the walk has run off the end, throws an invalid operation exception.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.LinkListEnumerator`1.MoveNext
member.summary: Steps the walk on to the next node, and on the first call onto the list's first node. Note that it decides it is on the first call by the walk standing nowhere, which is also the state it is left in once it has run off the end, so calling it again after it has returned false starts the walk over from the beginning instead of staying finished.
member.returns: true when the walk landed on a node, false when there was none left to land on.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Matrix3d.ArbitraryAxis(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes a matrix whose z axis lies along a given direction, picking the other two axes in the same settled way AutoCAD does, so that the same direction always gives the same frame. When the direction is close to straight up or down, within a sixty fourth in x and y, the world y axis is used to find the x axis, otherwise the world z axis is. member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d
member.summary: Offsets polylines, that is builds the curve running a fixed distance to one side of a poly. Two generations of the work live here side by side. The older one, reached through GetTrimmed, offsets both ways, unions the band that lies between the two into a forbidden area and keeps only the pieces of the wanted side that survive; the newer one, OffsetSpatial in the region at the bottom, offsets once, splits the result wherever it crosses itself and throws away every piece that ends up nearer the original than it should be. A positive distance offsets to one side of the direction of travel and a negative one to the other.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.GetTrimmed(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.OffsetGapType)
member.summary: Computes the offset of a poly with everything that folded back on itself cut away. The poly is offset in both directions, the band between the two offsets is unioned into a single area, and only the pieces of that area's outline that came from the wanted side are kept and joined back together. Note that it reads the tag of every arc coming out of the union as an integer, so it relies on the clipper carrying those tags through.
member.param: Poly to offset. It is not changed.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
Largest distance a corner may be carried away from the original vertex before it is cut off with a chamfer. Only used when the gap type is Extend.
How gaps at outer corners are bridged, by extending the two arcs until they meet or by rounding between them.
member.returns: A new region holding the trimmed offset. Empty when nothing of the offset survives.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.JoinArcs(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Arc2d})
member.summary: Joins loose arcs into polys by chaining each one onto a poly that already ends where it starts. Every poly is closed up afterwards if its two ends meet. Note that arcs are only ever matched end to start and never the other way round, so arcs arriving in an awkward order end up in separate polys that are never merged again.
member.param: Arcs to chain together. They are added by reference, not copied.
member.returns: A new region holding one poly per chain that could be built.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.GetForbiddenArea(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.OffsetGapType,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Builds the area that the offset is not allowed to enter, as one or more polys. For a closed poly this is the band between the offset on the wanted side and the offset the same distance the other way, the second of which is reversed so the two bound a ring. For an open poly it is a single closed outline around the whole poly, made by joining the two offsets with a half circle at each end. Note that the far side is always rounded, whatever gap type was asked for, and that the original direction of the poly is read into a local that is never used.
member.param: Poly to build the area around. It is not changed.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
Largest distance a corner may be carried from the original vertex before it is chamfered. Only used when the gap type is Extend.
How gaps at outer corners are bridged on the wanted side.
Set to the number of edges of the offset on the wanted side, which is what lets the caller tell those arcs apart from the ones bounding the far side.
member.returns: A new list of the polys bounding the forbidden area.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.GetUntrimmed(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.OffsetGapType)
member.summary: Computes the raw offset of a poly, with the gaps at outer corners bridged the way the given type asks for, and without cutting away anything that folds back on itself. An unknown gap type throws.
member.param: Poly to offset. It is not changed.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
Largest distance a corner may be carried from the original vertex before it is chamfered. Only used for the Extend type.
Extend to run the two arcs on until they meet, Round to swing an arc between them.
member.returns: A new poly holding the untrimmed offset.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.GetRawOffsetRound(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes the raw offset of a poly, rounding every outer corner with an arc swung about the original vertex. Each edge is offset on its own and consecutive pieces are then joined: where they cross, both are trimmed to the crossing; where one already reaches the other, they are snapped together; and where a gap is left, an arc is swung across it, turned inside out if it would sweep more than a hundred and eighty one degrees. Source edges shorter than 1e-3 are dropped altogether, so the result can have fewer pieces than the poly it came from, and nothing that folds back on itself is cut away here.
member.param: Poly to offset. It is not changed, although the arcs taken from it are.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side and also which way the corner arcs are swung.
member.returns: A new poly holding the untrimmed offset. Empty when every edge was too short to keep.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.MyOffset(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double)
member.summary: An earlier version of the rounded raw offset, kept for reference. Nothing calls it any more; the only mention left is the commented-out first line of GetRawOffsetRound, which is where it used to be called from. It differs from the version in use mainly in not holding back the trimming of the last piece of an open poly, so an open poly comes out with its final piece shortened.
member.param: Poly to offset.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
member.returns: A new poly holding the untrimmed offset.

The signed distance to offset orc.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.GetRawOffsetExtend(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Double},System.Double)
member.summary: Computes the raw offset of a poly where every edge may be offset by its own distance, running the offset pieces on until they meet rather than rounding the corners between them. One distance per edge, in edge order. The sign picks the side.
Largest distance a corner may be carried from the original vertex before it is cut off with a chamfer.

member.summary: Computes the raw offset of a poly by one distance for the whole poly, running the offset pieces on until they meet rather than rounding the corners between them. A copy of the poly is cleaned of near duplicate points first, so edges shorter than 1e-3 are gone before anything is offset. Nothing that folds back on itself is cut away here.
member.param: Poly to offset. A copy is worked on, so it is not changed.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
Largest distance a corner may be carried from the original vertex before it is cut off with a chamfer.
member.returns: A new poly holding the untrimmed offset.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.ExtendConnectArcs(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d@)
member.summary: Joins two neighbouring offset pieces at a corner, working in place on the two arcs handed in. Where the two run into each other the crossing is taken and both are trimmed to it. Where that crossing lies further from the original vertex than the largest distance allowed, and the corner turns outwards, a straight chamfer is cut across instead. Where they neither meet nor can be chamfered, an arc is swung between their loose ends, turned inside out if it would sweep more than a hundred and eighty one degrees, and a swung arc that comes out shorter than 1e-3 is thrown away again in favour of a single point on the bisector. Two pieces running in the same direction are always joined at the bisector point.
member.param: Offset piece running into the corner. Its end is moved.
The original edge a1 was offset from, used for its end tangent and vertex.
Offset piece running out of the corner. Its start is moved.
The original edge a2 was offset from, used for its start tangent.
Distance the pieces were offset by. The sign tells an inner corner from an outer one and which way a swung arc turns.
Largest distance the joint may sit from the original vertex before it is chamfered.
Set to a new arc or straight piece to put between the two, or to null when the two were simply trimmed to meet.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.IsOuterCorner(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Checks whether the corner between two edges turns away from the side being offset, which is the case where the offset leaves a gap that has to be bridged rather than an overlap that has to be trimmed. Two edges running in exactly the same direction give no answer on their own, so one of the two directions is nudged by a tenth of a radian according to which way its arc curves; two straight edges in line are reported as not an outer corner. Note that the cross product is worked out into a local that is then never read, the answer being computed a second time in the return.
member.param: Edge running into the corner, read only for which way it curves.
Direction of travel at the end of the first edge. It may be turned slightly by this method, which matters if a vector is a reference rather than a value.
Edge running out of the corner, read only for which way it curves.
Direction of travel at the start of the second edge. Reversed inside before use.
Distance being offset by. Only its sign is used.
member.returns: true when the corner turns away from the offset side, false when it turns into it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.ParametricallyClosestIntersection(IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,IGS.Genamo.Arc2d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Computes where two arcs cross, taking both as unbounded, and picks between two crossings by where they fall along the second arc rather than by distance. At an outer corner the wanted crossing lies before the start of the second piece, so the largest parameter below zero is taken; at an inner corner the smallest parameter from zero upwards is taken instead. A parameter beyond the end of the arc is first reinterpreted as a negative one on the far side, so that the two can be compared on one scale.

member.returns: The chosen crossing, or null when the two do not cross at all.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSpatial(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.Poly2d@)
member.summary: Computes the offset of a poly with everything that folded back on itself cut away, by the newer route. The poly is offset once, the pieces are joined into a single outline, that outline is cut apart wherever it crosses itself, every piece that ends up nearer the original poly than the offset distance is thrown away, and what is left is chained back together. The untrimmed outline is handed back as well, which is useful when the result looks wrong.
member.param: Poly to offset. Not changed here, although the outline built from it is.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
Set to the untrimmed outline, before anything was cut away. Empty when the poly had nothing long enough to offset.
member.returns: A new region holding the trimmed offset, one poly per surviving chain. Empty when nothing survives.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.JoinChains(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d})
member.summary: Chains loose polys together end to end and closes up each chain that comes back to its own start. Whenever a poly is added the scan starts over, since the growing chain now ends somewhere else and polys already passed over may fit. Note that pieces are only matched end to start, so a piece that would fit the other way round is left on its own.
member.param: Polys to chain together. The list itself is not changed, but the polys in it are added to.
member.returns: A new list holding one poly per chain that could be built.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.CalculateOffsetSegments(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Offsets every edge of a poly on its own and records each result together with the direction of travel at both of its ends. Edges shorter than epsilon are skipped, so the result can hold fewer pieces than the poly has edges. An arc whose radius the offset drove through zero is marked as collapsed, since the piece it leaves curves the other way from the edge it came from.
member.param: Poly to offset. It is not changed.
Distance to offset by. The sign picks the side.
member.returns: A new list of the offset pieces, in edge order.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.ConnectOffsetSegments(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSegment},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Walks the offset pieces in order and bridges the gap at every corner between them, giving back the pieces and the bridges as one list. On a closed poly the last piece is also joined back to the first; on an open one it is simply added at the end. The list handed in must not be empty.
member.param: Offset pieces in edge order. The pieces are changed in place where a corner is trimmed.
true when the poly was closed, so that the last and first pieces are joined as well.
member.returns: A new list holding the pieces and the bridges between them, in order.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.ConnectPair(IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSegment,IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSegment,System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSegment})
member.summary: Bridges the gap between two neighbouring offset pieces, appending the first piece and, where one is needed, a bridge between them. Ends that already meet are snapped to their midpoint. Otherwise an arc is swung from one to the other; if that arc would sweep more than half a turn the corner is really an inner one, so the two pieces are trimmed to where they cross instead, and only if that fails is a straight piece laid across. Note that the first piece is appended before it may be trimmed, which works because the pieces are held by reference.
member.param: Piece running into the corner. Its end may be moved.
Piece running out of the corner. Its start may be moved.
List the first piece and any bridge are appended to.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.TryTrimInnerCorner(IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSegment,IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.OffsetSegment)
member.summary: Trims two neighbouring offset pieces back to where they cross, which is what an inner corner needs. Where they cross twice the crossing nearer the original vertex is taken. Both pieces are changed in place.
member.param: Piece running into the corner. Its end is moved to the crossing.
Piece running out of the corner. Its start is moved to the crossing.
member.returns: true when a crossing was found and both pieces were trimmed, false when they do not cross and nothing was changed.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.FindSelfIntersections(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d)
member.summary: Finds every place where an outline runs into itself, as a list of edge index and parameter along that edge. The edges are put in a spatial index so that only pairs whose boxes overlap are actually crossed, and the work is spread over several threads. Each pair is tested only once, in index order. Crossings sitting exactly at the start of an edge are left out, and so are the ones at the shared end of two neighbouring edges, since those are joints rather than crossings. The result is sorted by edge and then by parameter, and near duplicates are removed. Note that the outline is closed up in place before anything else is done.
member.param: Outline to search. Closed up in place.
member.returns: A new list of crossings, each as the edge index and the parameter along that edge, sorted and free of duplicates.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.SplitToChains(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.ValueTuple{System.Int32,System.Double}})
member.summary: Cuts an outline apart at a list of crossings and gives back the pieces between them. The crossings must already be sorted by edge and by parameter, which is how FindSelfIntersections hands them over. The walk starts at the beginning of the first edge, so on a closed outline the piece running across that point comes back as two chains rather than one; joining those again is left to JoinChains. A trailing piece shorter than epsilon is dropped.
member.param: Outline to cut apart. It is not changed.
Crossings to cut at, as edge index and parameter, sorted.
member.returns: A new list of the pieces between the crossings, in order along the outline.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.RemoveInvalidChains(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d},IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Throws away the pieces of a cut up offset that ended up on the wrong side, that is nearer the original poly than the offset distance. The original poly's edges go into a spatial index and each piece is then judged, over several threads, by a single point taken from its middle. Note that one point decides the whole piece, so a piece that is partly too near and partly not is kept or dropped as a whole.
member.param: Pieces to judge. The list is not changed.
The poly that was offset, measured against.
Distance that was offset by. Only its size is used.
member.returns: A new list holding the pieces that survived, in their original order.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.IsPointValid(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.SpatialIndex2d,System.Collections.Generic.Stack{System.Int32})
member.summary: Checks whether a point lies far enough from a poly to belong to its offset, that is no nearer than the offset distance less a thousandth. Only the edges whose boxes reach the point are measured, and the walk stops at the first edge that comes too near.
member.param: Poly to measure against.
Offset distance, without its sign.
Point to judge.
Spatial index over the poly's edges, already finished.
Scratch space for the index walk, one per thread.
member.returns: true when no edge comes nearer than the distance allows, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Offset2d.IsAdjacentSeg(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Checks whether two edges of an outline are neighbours, and so share an end point rather than really crossing. On a closed outline the first and last edges are neighbours too. The two indices must be handed in with the smaller one first.

The larger of the two edge indices.
Number of edges in the outline.
true when the outline is closed, so that the last edge meets the first.
member.returns: true when the two edges are neighbours, otherwise false.

member.summary: Adds an object to the scan process. Objects with same setIndex is not tested against each other. The boundingbox considered is grown with extraInflate so that nearby ojects can be found.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.OverScan3d`1
member.summary: Finds overlapping bounding boxes in three dimensions, in the same way as OverScan2d does in the plane. Note that only two of the three directions are actually checked: the sweep covers the one the point ordering sorts by, and the open boxes are then compared on x alone, so two boxes that overlap in those two but lie well apart in the third are still reported. A callback that needs a real overlap has to test the remaining direction itself.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ParallelOLD
member.summary: A hand written parallel for loop, from before the framework offered one of its own. The name says what it is: the newer code in this library calls System.Threading.Tasks.Parallel instead, and the note at the top of the body asks for this to be cleaned up. It is also tied to the .NET Framework, since it starts its workers by calling BeginInvoke on a delegate, which later runtimes refuse.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternInfo.ScorePoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Compute how well a point fits this pattern. Returns the spatial distance (residual) from the point to the nearest expected position in the pattern. Lower = better fit. Returns double.MaxValue for Scattered patterns.
member.param: Point to measure against the pattern.
member.returns: The distance from the point to the nearest place this pattern would put it, or double.MaxValue for a scattered pattern and for any pattern whose geometry was never filled in.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternInfo.ScoreGridPoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes how far a point lies from the nearest place the lattice would put it. The point is turned into lattice coordinates through the two basis vectors, rounded to the nearest whole cell, and the leftover is measured back in model units. On a staggered lattice both readings are tried, with the shift on odd rows and with it on even rows, and the smaller of the two is taken.
member.param: Point to measure.
member.returns: The distance from the point to the nearest lattice position, or double.MaxValue when the lattice was never filled in or its two basis vectors lie along one another.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternInfo.ScoreRadialPoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes how far a point lies from the nearest ring. When the individual ring radii were recorded the point is measured against each of them and the smallest difference is taken; otherwise the even ring spacing is used and the point is measured against the nearest whole number of rings out from the centre. Only the distance from the centre matters here, so where the point sits around the ring makes no difference.
member.param: Point to measure.
member.returns: The distance from the point to the nearest ring, or double.MaxValue when neither a set of radii nor a usable spacing was recorded.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternInfo.ScoreLinePoint(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes how far a point lies from the line, measured at right angles to it. The line is taken as infinite, so a point well beyond either end of the run of shapes still scores as being on it.
member.param: Point to measure.
member.returns: The distance from the point to the line, or double.MaxValue when the line was never filled in.
