member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector
member.summary:
Detects geometric patterns (grids, arcs, radial, scattered) in sets of 2D shapes.
ARCHITECTURE: 1. Shape-aware MST clustering (Distance2d.PolyPoly + ExtentsExtents) 2. Per-cluster density sub-clustering (NN distance bimodality) 3. Per-density-group spatial re-clustering (centroid MST with smart fragment merge) 4. Per-group single-pass pattern CLASSIFICATION: - ALL detectors run on the group - Best-fitting type wins → ALL points assigned to that pattern - No iterative splitting — clustering handles separation 5. Small/singleton clusters → Scattered

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.DetectPatterns(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings)
member.summary: Main entry point. Detects all patterns in the given shapes.
member.param: Shapes to look through. Only their outlines and their middle points are read; nothing is changed.
Thresholds and the optional trace callback. Pass null to use the defaults.
member.returns: A new list holding one entry per pattern found, plus one scattered entry gathering the shapes that belonged to no pattern. Empty only when no shapes were handed in.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.TryDensitySplit(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings)
member.summary: Checks if a cluster contains shapes at different density scales by analyzing the nearest-neighbor distance distribution. If the NN distances are bimodal (e.g., tight grid at 1mm + radial at 7mm), splits into separate groups so each can be detected independently. Returns null if no clear density split is found.
member.param: Middle point of every shape, indexed globally.
The shapes of this cluster, as indices into allCentroids.
Thresholds and the trace callback.
member.returns: A new list of groups, already broken apart again by position within each density, or null when no clear split in the neighbour distances was found or one side of it would be too small.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.SpatialSubCluster(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings)
member.summary: Splits a group of shapes into spatially separated sub-groups using a lightweight centroid-based MST with jump detection. Returns the input as a single group if no clear spatial gap is found.
member.param: Middle point of every shape, indexed globally.
The shapes to split, as indices into allCentroids.
Thresholds and the trace callback.
member.returns: A new list of sub-groups. Groups too small to stand on their own are gathered back into one, and the whole input comes back as a single group when no clear gap was found, when cutting at it would break more than a fifth of the links, or when nothing survived the split.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.DetectPatternsInCluster(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Classify a group of shapes as a single pattern. After MST clustering → density split → spatial re-clustering, each group is expected to be ONE pattern. We run all detectors and pick the best-fitting type, assigning ALL points to it. No iterative splitting — clustering handles separation.
member.param: Middle point of every shape, indexed globally.
The shapes of this group, as indices into allCentroids.
Thresholds and the trace callback.
true to try breaking the group apart by density first. Set false on the recursive calls, so that the splitting is only ever tried once.
member.returns: A new list holding one pattern per group, or a single scattered pattern when no detector fitted. Every shape handed in appears in exactly one of them, since the winning detector takes the whole group whatever share of it actually matched.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.MSTCluster(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d},IGS.Genamo.Extents2d[],System.Int32,IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings)
member.summary: Clusters shapes using real contour-to-contour distances. Uses ExtentsExtents as fast lower bound to skip expensive PolyPoly calls.
member.param: Shapes to cluster. Nothing is changed.
Bounding box of every shape, in the same order, used as the cheap lower bound.
Number of shapes.
Thresholds and the trace callback.
member.returns: A new list of clusters, largest first, each holding the indices of its shapes. One cluster holding everything when no gap was clear enough to cut at.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.TryDetectRadial(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings)
member.summary:
Detects radial / concentric ring patterns. Estimates the center, then identifies concentric rings via distance histogram, and verifies angular regularity within each ring.
This is crucial for patterns like drains, turbines, flanges etc. where shapes are arranged in concentric rings around a center point.
member.param: Middle point of every shape, indexed globally.
The shapes to look at, as indices into allCentroids.
Thresholds and the trace callback.
member.returns: A new pattern holding the centre, the ring radii and the spoke count, or null when too few rings were found, when the centre could not be estimated, or when too few of the shapes ended up on a ring.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.EstimateRadialCenter(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Int32)
member.summary:
Estimates the center of a radial pattern.
Primary: centroid of all points. For any roughly symmetric radial pattern (drains, turbines, flanges) the centroid IS the center.
Secondary: if centroid doesn't find rings, try circumcircle voting from nearby triplets (same-ring points give the exact center).
member.param: Points of the pattern.
Number of points.
member.returns: A new point at the average of them all, or null when there are fewer than three. Note that the body only ever works out that average: the circumcircle voting the summary mentions is a separate method that the caller runs afterwards in every case, not only when this one fails.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.TryCircumcircleCenter(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Int32,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Attempts to refine a radial center using circumcircle voting from nearby triplets. Only nearby points (likely same ring) are used as triplets. Returns null if insufficient data.
member.param: Points of the pattern.
Number of points. Fewer than six gives up at once.
Centre to measure candidates against; one lying further from it than half the spread of the points is thrown out.
Typical distance to a nearest neighbour. Points within two and a half times it are taken as belonging to the same ring.
member.returns: A new point at the median of the circle centres that survived, or null when fewer than ten of them did. The random picking is seeded to a fixed value, so the same points always give the same answer.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.RefineRadialCenter(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32}},IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Refine center using iterative adjustment to minimize intra-ring distance variance.
member.param: Points of the pattern.
The rings, each holding indices into the points. Only points that landed on a ring take part.
Centre to start from. It is not changed.
member.returns: A new point at the best centre found, or the starting point itself when the rings hold no usable radius to scale the steps by.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.ComputeRingVariance(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32}},System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Compute sum of intra-ring distance variance for a candidate center. Used by RefineRadialCenter.
member.param: Points of the pattern.
The rings, each holding indices into the points. A ring with fewer than two points is skipped.
X of the centre to try.
Y of the centre to try.
member.returns: The variances of the rings added together. Lower means the points of each ring sit at a more even distance from the centre.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.TryDetectGrid(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings)
member.summary: Tries to detect a grid (regular, staggered, or hexagonal).
member.param: Middle point of every shape, indexed globally.
The shapes to look at, as indices into allCentroids.
Thresholds and the trace callback.
member.returns: A new pattern holding the two basis vectors, the stagger and the row and column counts, or null when there are fewer than four points, when the neighbour distances vary too much to be a grid at all, when no direction stood out, or when no lattice caught at least four points.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.EstimateBasisLength(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Int32,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Works out how far apart the lattice steps are along one direction, by measuring every pair of points that lies roughly along that direction and finding the distance that turns up most often. Only pairs between a third and three times the typical neighbour distance are considered, so that a step of two or three cells does not drown out the real one. The winning distance is then the average of everything close to it rather than the single most common value.
member.param: Points to measure between.
Number of points.
Direction to measure along, in radians, taken without regard to which way round it points. Pairs within fifteen degrees of it count.
Typical distance to a nearest neighbour, used both to bound which pairs count and as the answer when none do.
Not used.
member.returns: The step length along that direction, or the typical neighbour distance when no pair lay along it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.FitLattice(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Int32,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,IGS.Genamo.Vector2d,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Tries a lattice built from two basis vectors against a set of points, and reports how well the best placing of it fits. Every point in turn, up to twenty of them spread through the set, is tried as the lattice origin, and for each the points are turned into lattice coordinates, rounded to the nearest cell and measured back in model units; whichever origin catches the most points wins. A staggered lattice allows a point to sit either on the plain grid or on the shifted one.
member.param: Points to fit the lattice to.
Number of points.
First basis vector, giving one lattice direction and its step length.
Second basis vector, giving the other lattice direction and its step length.
Largest distance in model units a point may sit from its lattice position and still count as on the lattice.
Fraction of the first basis vector that odd rows are shifted by. Zero for a plain lattice.
member.returns: The best fit found, holding how many points it caught, which ones, the spread of rows and columns, and the origin it was built about.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.TryDetectArcOrLine(IGS.Genamo.Point2d[],System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int32},IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings,System.Int32)
member.summary: Tries to detect a dominant arc or line using RANSAC.
member.param: Middle point of every shape, indexed globally.
The shapes to look at, as indices into allCentroids.
Thresholds and the trace callback, including how many tries to make and how flat an arc may be before it is rejected.
Fewest points a line or an arc must gather to count.
member.returns: A new pattern for whichever of the two fitted better, the line winning ties within a tenth, or null when neither gathered enough points. The random picking is seeded to a fixed value, so the same points always give the same answer.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PatternDetector.Log(IGS.Genamo.PatternDetectorSettings,System.String,System.Object[])

The second point of the infinite line to intersect with this plane

member.summary: True if the point is on the plane, within a given tolerance.

How far from the plane the point may lie and still count as on it. It is compared against the point's dot product with the normal, so it is a true distance only where the normal is of unit length.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.Origo
member.summary: Gets a new point at the plane's own origin. It is a copy, so changing what comes back does not move the plane.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.Normal
member.summary: Gets a new vector along the plane's normal. It is a copy, so changing what comes back does not turn the plane. The vector is handed back exactly as it was given to the constructor and is never normalised, so anything measured against it, such as the tolerances in PointInPlane and Side or the value of D, is scaled by its length.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.Side(IGS.Genamo.Point3d,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes a side of a point relative the plane. If the point is on the same side as the normal points to, Side.Right is returned. If the point is within 'tol' tolerance on the plane (in a dot product) Side.On is returned. Else Side.Left is returned.
member.param: Point to place. A point sitting on the plane origin itself always gives On.

How near the plane the point may lie and still count as on it. The direction to the point is normalised first but the plane normal is not, so this behaves as a limit on the sine of the angle from the plane, scaled by the normal's length, rather than as a distance.
member.returns: Right when the point lies on the side the normal points to, Left when it lies on the other side, and On when it lies within the tolerance of the plane.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.ClosestPoint(IGS.Genamo.Point3d)

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.D
member.summary: Gets the constant term of the plane equation, that is the normal dotted with the origin. A point lies on the plane when its own dot product with the normal equals this. Like everything else built from the normal it is scaled by the normal's length, so it is a true distance from world origo only where the normal is of unit length.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.SignedAngle(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d)
member.summary: Computes the angle between a vector and the plane, taking a right angle to the normal as zero. It is positive where the vector leans towards the side the normal points to and negative where it leans away, which is what makes it signed.

member.summary: Computes the angle between a vector and the plane without regard to which side it leans towards.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.CreateMatrix
member.summary: Builds the two matrices that turn plane coordinates into world coordinates and back, and stores them on the plane. The local z axis is the plane normal and the local origin is the plane origin; the local x axis is found by dropping one of the two world axes onto the plane and keeping whichever of them lands further from the origin, so that a plane standing on edge still gets a well behaved frame. Project and PointAt call this on their own the first time they are needed, so it rarely has to be called from outside; calling it again rebuilds both matrices.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.Project(IGS.Genamo.Point3d)
member.summary: Turns a point of the plane into the two coordinates that locate it within the plane. The point is taken into the plane's own frame and its distance along the normal is simply dropped, so a point that does not really lie on the plane is quietly flattened onto it rather than refused. Builds the plane's matrices on the first call.
member.param: Point to turn into plane coordinates. It is not changed.
member.returns: A new point holding the two coordinates within the plane.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.PointAt(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Turns two coordinates within the plane back into a point in space. This undoes what Project does, except that anything Project dropped is gone. Builds the plane's matrices on the first call.
member.param: The two coordinates within the plane.
member.returns: A new point in world coordinates lying on the plane.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.Matrix
member.summary: Turns plane coordinates into world coordinates. Null until the first call to CreateMatrix, and set back to null whenever the plane is moved. Public, so it can be replaced from outside, in which case nothing keeps it in step with the plane's own origin and normal.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.MatrixInv

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Plane3d.Transform(IGS.Genamo.Matrix3d)
member.summary: Moves the plane by a matrix, in place. The origin is carried through the matrix as a point and the normal as a normal, which is not the same thing where the matrix stretches or shears, and the two cached matrices are thrown away so that they are built again from the new position. Being internal, this is the only way the plane can be moved, and it is not open to code outside the library.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PlaneSweepEvent.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Orders two events by where they sit in the plane, by y first and then by x, which is the order the sweep runs in. Two events at the same spot keep the order they were added in, since the sort is stable, and that is what guarantees an object's opening event is always reached before its closing one. It assumes the object really is an event, so anything else gives a cast or null reference error rather than the argument exception a comparer normally raises.
member.param: Event to compare with. Must be an event of this same type.
member.returns: Minus one when this event comes first in sweep order, one when it comes after, and zero when the two sit at the same spot.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Pocketer
member.summary: Builds the tool paths that clear out the inside of a region, as a set of zigzag passes. The region is cut by a family of horizontal lines one unit apart, the pieces of boundary between the cuts are gathered up, and a walk then joins them into as few continuous paths as it can, always moving upwards. An angle and a spacing can be given, in which case the region is turned and scaled so that the fixed unit spacing lands where the caller wanted it and the result is turned back again.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Pocketer.Pocket(IGS.Genamo.Region2d)
member.summary: Computes the pocketing paths for a region, with the passes running horizontally one unit apart.
member.param: Region to clear out. Its polys are read but not changed.
member.returns: A new list of paths, each a poly running from one side of the region to the other and back. Empty when the region gave nothing to cut.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Pocketer.Pocket(IGS.Genamo.Region2d,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes the pocketing paths for a region with the passes at a chosen angle and spacing. The region is copied, turned so that the wanted angle lies flat and scaled so that the wanted spacing becomes one unit, since the cutting itself always works on whole numbered rows; the paths that come back are scaled and turned to match the region as it was handed in.
member.param: Region to clear out. It is copied first, so it is not changed.
Direction the passes are to run in, in radians.
Distance between two passes. Zero makes the scaling divide by zero.
member.returns: A new list of paths in the region's own coordinates.

member.summary: Computes where one whole numbered row crosses an edge. An end of the edge lying on the row counts as a crossing in its own right. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Point3d.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Orders two points by x first, then by y, then by z. Note two things about it. It is x first, where the 2d point orders by y first, so sorting the two kinds of point does not give the same sweep direction. And each coordinate is first tested for equality within the default tolerance and only then compared exactly, which means the ordering is not consistent: two points can each count as level with a third and yet not with each other, which is enough to make a sort misbehave or throw.
member.param: Point to compare with. Anything that is not a 3d point raises an argument exception.
member.returns: Minus one when this point comes first, one when it comes after, and zero when the two are the same point within the tolerance.

member.summary: Rounds the coordinates of every node in the poly in-place to the given number of decimals. Only the x and y values are rounded, the bulges are left untouched, which means an arc segment keeps its bulge but gets slightly different endpoints and therefore a slightly different radius. member.summary: Computes a new poly which is an offset of this poly. The offsetted segments can be joined with an arc or by extension. This function automatically removes trivial (zero length) segments in the result poly. The resulting poly will _not_ be trimmed and may contain loops. Use Union() or Trim() to remove such loops if needed.
member.param: The distance to offset the poly. Posetive value offsetts to the right and nagative to the left.
The type of joins made between offsetted segments of poly. See OffsetGapType enumeration for details.
Only used if gaptype is Extend. This is the maximum distance two segments might be extended, otherwise a chamfer is created. If gaptype is not Extend, this parameter is not used.
member.returns: A new, offsetted poly.

member.summary: Detects if a node in a poly is an outside corner. Poly is supposed to be closed and CCW.

The "turn angle", If angle is larger than this is counted as a corner.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly2d.IsOuterCornerAtParam(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Checks if the poly makes an outer corner at a given parameter. The tangent is evaluated 1e-6 before and 1e-6 after the parameter and the counter clockwise sweep from the reversed incoming tangent to the outgoing tangent is measured. That sweep is exactly PI where the poly runs straight through, so the test is true when the poly turns counter clockwise, to the left, by more than angle radians. The poly is supposed to be closed and CCW, where a left turn is a convex corner of the enclosed material. Unlike IsOuterCorner there is no direction flag, CCW is assumed. The 1e-6 step is in parameter space, so the sampled distance is 1e-6 of the total length and a segment shorter than that can be stepped over. Throws if the poly is empty.
member.param: The parameter to check, in the range 0-1 along the poly. Values outside the range wrap around on a closed poly.
The turn angle limit in radians. A turn larger than this counts as a corner.
member.returns: True if the poly turns counter clockwise by more than angle at the parameter, false otherwise.

When the poly is empty, or the line starts further than Calc.Epsilon from the current end node, the line's start is added as a node of its own; otherwise the current end node is moved onto the line's start rather than a duplicate being added, which edits that node where it sits. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Add(IGS.Genamo.Poly3d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Appends another poly's nodes to this one, in place. Does nothing when the other poly is empty. When this poly already has nodes and either forceendpoints is set or the other poly starts within Calc.Epsilon of the current end node, that end node is moved onto the other poly's start and takes its tag, instead of a duplicate node being added; otherwise the start is appended as a new node. The remaining nodes follow, and for a closed source poly its first node is appended once more to close that run. This poly's own closed flag is left as it was.
member.param: Poly whose nodes are appended. Its nodes are copied, not shared.
True to weld the two ends together however far apart they are, false to weld them only when they lie within Calc.Epsilon of each other.

member.summary: Closes the poly in place when its two ends already meet. Does nothing when the poly is closed already, or when start and end lie further apart than acc. When they are close enough the last node is removed and the closed flag set, since a closed poly does not repeat its first node.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Eval(System.Double,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d@)
member.summary: Computes the point at a parameter along the poly and the direction there. The poly is parameterized from zero to one by arc length, so the parameter is the fraction of the total length walked from the start. Throws an exception when the poly has no nodes. A parameter outside zero to one is wrapped back into range for a closed poly, while for an open one the poly is extended along the direction of its first or last segment, so the point returned then lies off the poly. A poly of a single node gives a copy of that node and a zero tangent.
member.param: Position along the poly, as a fraction of its total length.
Set to the normalized direction of the segment the parameter falls on.
member.returns: A new point at that position.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Param(IGS.Genamo.Point3d)
member.summary: Computes the parameter of a point lying on the poly, as the fraction of the total length walked from the start to reach it. The first segment that passes within 1e-4 of the point decides the answer, so a point at a self intersection gets the earlier of the two parameters. Throws an exception when the poly has no nodes, and also when the point lies further than 1e-4 from every segment. A poly of one node, or one whose total length is below 1e-9, gives zero.
member.param: Point on the poly to find the parameter of.
member.returns: The parameter, between zero and one.

member.summary: Gets a reference to the node at an index, or replaces that node with a copy of a given point. The index is wrapped with Calc.Mod, so negative and too large indices count round the list instead of throwing. Throws an ArgumentException when the poly has no nodes. Since the getter hands out the node itself, writing to the point returned changes the poly.
member.param: Index of the node, wrapped into range.
member.returns: A reference to the node at that index.

For a closed poly it equals the node count, because of the closing segment, except that a poly of one node or none has no segments at all. Both indices are taken modulo the node count, so the last segment of a closed poly runs from the last node back to the first. The line copies the two nodes, so changing it does not change the poly. As written it never says yes: the inner test only lets the counter grow once the counter has already reached one, and nothing else ever raises it, so it stays at zero and the method answers false for every poly.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Measure(System.Double)
member.summary: Walks the poly and returns a new list of points spaced about d apart. The spacing restarts at every segment, so points bunch up around the nodes and only the spacing within one segment is really d. Segments shorter than 1e-9 are skipped, and a segment no longer than d contributes only its start point. The end of the poly is not included.
member.param: Wanted distance between points.
member.returns: A new list of new points along the poly.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Measure2(System.Double)
member.summary: Walks the poly and returns a new list of points spaced d apart, carrying the running distance across the node boundaries so the spacing holds along the whole poly instead of segment by segment. The first point is the start of the poly; the end is not included. A d of zero or less never advances the running distance and loops forever.
member.param: Distance between points.
member.returns: A new list of new points along the poly.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Measure3(System.Double)
member.summary: Walks the poly like Measure2, but first stretches the spacing so a whole number of steps fits the total length, and appends the end point when it is done. When the poly is shorter than d the step count comes out zero and the spacing becomes infinite, which leaves only the end point in the result.
member.param: Wanted distance between points, stretched up so it divides the total length a whole number of times.
member.returns: A new list of new points along the poly, ending at its end point.

member.summary: Removes nodes sitting closer than acc to the node kept before them, in place. Does nothing at all for a poly of fewer than three nodes. The first node is always kept. When the last surviving node ends up within acc of the first it is not removed but moved onto the first, which leaves the contour with its start point repeated at the end. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Split(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Double})
member.summary: Cuts the poly at the given parameters and returns the pieces as new polys, leaving this poly alone. The parameters are sorted first, so they may be given in any order, and each is a fraction of the total length the way Eval reads one. Pieces of fewer than two nodes are dropped and zero length segments are left out, except inside a segment that is itself being cut. For a closed poly giving two or more pieces the last piece is joined onto the front of the first, so the result starts at the first cut rather than at the poly's own start point. All the pieces returned are open.
member.param: Parameters to cut at, each between zero and one.
member.returns: A new list of new polys covering the poly in order.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.SubPoly(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Copies out the stretch of the poly beginning at one parameter and running on for a given length, both measured as fractions of the total length, and returns it as a new poly. A start above one is wrapped back into range. A negative length means the stretch runs backwards from the start parameter, and the result is reversed before it is handed back so it still runs that way. The walk over the segments wraps around with the index, so an open poly is treated as if it were closed and a stretch running off the end carries on from the beginning. Nothing bounds the walk except reaching the end parameter, so a poly of zero length loops forever.
member.param: Parameter to start at, as a fraction of the total length.
Length of the stretch, as a fraction of the total length. Negative to run backwards from the start parameter.
member.returns: A new poly holding that stretch.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.Split(System.Double[])
member.summary: Cuts the poly at the given parameters and returns the pieces as new polys. Convenience form that takes the parameters loose rather than in a list and hands them to the other Split.
member.param: Parameters to cut at, each between zero and one.
member.returns: A new list of new polys covering the poly in order.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.DouglasPeucker(System.Double)
member.summary: Simplifies the poly with the Douglas Peucker method and returns the result as a new poly, leaving this one alone. The two ends are kept and the node furthest from the chord between them is put back whenever it lies further away than tol, recursively. For a closed poly the far end is the node past the last one, which the wrapping indexer turns back into the start node, so the result both repeats the start point at the end and is marked closed, which is not how a closed poly is stored anywhere else. Throws an ArgumentException when the poly has no nodes.
member.param: Largest distance a node may sit from the simplified line and still be dropped.
member.returns: A new poly with the same ends and a subset of the nodes between them.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Poly3d.RecursiveInsert(IGS.Genamo.Poly3d,System.Int32,System.Int32,IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.Point3d},IGS.Genamo.LinkListNode{IGS.Genamo.Point3d},IGS.Genamo.LinkListNode{IGS.Genamo.Point3d},System.Double)
member.summary: One step of the Douglas Peucker simplification. Finds the node between two indices lying furthest from the straight line between the two nodes already kept, and when it is at least tol away inserts it into the list in front of the later of the two and recurses into the two halves that makes. Distance is measured to the segment between the kept nodes, not to the infinite line through them.
member.param: Poly whose nodes are being looked at. Read through the wrapping indexer, so an end index equal to the node count means the start node again.
Index of the node already kept at the start of this stretch.
Index of the node already kept at the end of this stretch.
List of kept nodes being built, in order.
List node holding the kept node at the start of this stretch.
List node holding the kept node at the end of this stretch. New nodes are inserted in front of it.
Smallest distance from the chord that still makes a node worth keeping.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d
member.summary: Boolean operations on 2d regions of arcs and lines: union, non zero union and intersection. All three work the same way, in three steps. Every poly is cut at every intersection it has with any other, each piece is then tested once to decide whether it lies on the boundary of the answer, and the pieces that survive are stitched back into closed loops. The polys handed in are changed along the way, since the steps clean them and, with optimize set, rotate them.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.FastInsideArc
member.summary: Holds the arcs of a cut up arrangement in an interval tree keyed on their y range, and answers, one arc at a time, whether that arc lies on the boundary of the union or of the intersection. The test is a ray cast to the left from a point on the arc: the arcs whose y range covers that height are pulled out of the tree, the crossings to the left of the probe are counted, and the count decides. Add every arc first, then ask.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.FastInsideArc.FPos.Classify(IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.FastInsideArc.FArc,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Works out where and how an arc crosses the horizontal line through a point, and whether that crossing counts at all. A horizontal arc is always reported, placed at the middle of its own span. For any other arc a crossing at a shared end point is only counted when the arc leaves that height upwards, the usual half open rule that stops a shared node being counted twice; forceadd overrides it so the arc being tested is always classified. An arc lying wholly to the left of the point is given the left edge of its bounding box instead of its real crossing, since the exact value cannot change the count. The direction is taken from the straight line between the arc's end points and not from the true tangent, so for a curved arc it is only an approximation.
member.param: Arc to classify.
Point the ray runs through. Its y places the crossing, its x is used only to decide whether the arc lies wholly to the left.
Position in the arrangement to record on the crossing.
True to report the crossing even where the half open rule would drop it.
member.returns: A new crossing record, or null when the arc does not count at this height.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.FastInsideArc.FPos.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Orders two crossings along the ray: by position first, with anything within 1e-4 counting as the same spot, then left hand edges before right hand ones, then by decreasing direction angle, and last by position in the arrangement. Because the position test is tolerant while the tie breakers are exact the ordering is not transitive, so it is safe for comparing one crossing against another as the code does here but not for sorting a list of them. Anything that is not a crossing record gives a null reference error rather than the argument exception a comparer usually raises.
member.param: The other crossing to compare against. Must be an FPos.
member.returns: Minus one when this crossing comes first along the ray, one when it comes after, and zero when the two agree on position, side, angle and arrangement index.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.FastInsideArc.FPos.KeepEdgeNonZero(System.Int32)
member.summary: Decides from the crossing count whether an edge lies on the boundary under the non zero fill rule, which unlike the plain union rule keeps the hole cut by a loop running the other way round. member.param: Crossings counted to the left of the edge, left hand edges counting plus one and right hand edges minus one.
member.returns: True to keep the edge, false to drop it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.Union(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d},System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Unions a list of polys into one another and returns the result as a new region. Every poly is cut at every intersection it has with any of the others, each piece is tested once to see whether it lies on the outside of everything, and the surviving pieces are stitched back into closed loops. A piece that closes on itself with an area below 1e-4 is thrown away as noise. The arc used to probe a piece is the one spanning the most height, a nearly horizontal arc making a poor probe. With optimize set the whole problem is first rotated into a direction that leaves fewer awkward cases and the pieces are tested in parallel; the result is rotated back afterwards, but the polys handed in are left rotated.
member.param: Polys to union. Changed in place: cleaned, and rotated as well when optimize is set. The list itself is not changed.
True to rotate the problem into a better direction for the sweep and test the pieces in parallel.
True to fill by the non zero rule, false by the plain union rule.
member.returns: A new region holding the union.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.Join(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d})
member.summary: Stitches loose pieces back into closed loops and returns them as a new region. Starting from the first piece it repeatedly looks for whichever remaining piece begins nearest the loop's open end, and adds it while that start is both nearer than the loop's own start point and within 1e-3; otherwise it closes the loop off with a tolerance of 1e-3 and begins a new one. Loops of a single edge, and loops no longer than Calc.Epsilon, are thrown away. The list handed in is emptied as the pieces are used.
member.param: Pieces to stitch. Emptied by the call.
member.returns: A new region holding the loops that were made.

Pieces to search. Must hold at least one.
member.returns: Index into the list of the nearest piece.

member.summary: Rotates every poly in place into the direction that suits the sweep best, and reports the angle it turned them by. The direction comes from the smallest enclosing rectangle of all the nodes: the polys are turned so that rectangle's longer side stands vertical, and then a further 0.01 radians so no edge is left exactly axis aligned. Turning the answer back by the negative of the angle returned is left to the caller, and the polys themselves are never turned back.
member.param: Polys to rotate. Changed in place.
Not used. The value is overwritten before it is ever read.
member.returns: The angle in radians the polys were turned by.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolyClip2d.FindIntersections(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d})
member.summary: Finds every place the polys cross each other or themselves, and returns for each poly the parameters along it at which it should be cut. A sweep over the bounding boxes narrows the work down to the pairs of edges that can possibly meet, and each such pair is then intersected exactly. Where two edges do not properly cross but one ends on the other within Calc.Epsilon, that touch is recorded as a crossing as well. The node two neighbouring edges of the same poly share is left out. The parameters come back in the order they were found rather than sorted, and the same place can appear more than once. Every poly is cleaned in place first, which rounds its coordinates to six decimals.
member.param: Polys to search. Cleaned in place.
member.returns: A new list holding one list of parameters per poly, in the same order as the polys, each parameter a fraction of that poly's length.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification
member.summary: Removes vertices from a polygon while keeping its shape, by repeatedly taking away whichever vertex costs the least area. Two methods live here. Calculate is the careful one: it never lets the result cross itself, it can straighten an outside corner by extending its two edges to where they meet rather than only cutting corners off, and it finishes by pushing each surviving edge out against the original outline. Simplify is the cheap one, with no crossing test at all.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.UpdateEdge(IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.SimplifyNode,IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.SimplifyNode})
member.summary: Pushes one edge of the simplified poly out against the original outline, changing the two vertices in place. It gathers the original vertices this edge has swallowed, together with the neighbour on either side, and measures each against the infinite line through the edge. When every one of them is more than 1e-6 away the edge is moved sideways by the smallest of those distances and re-intersected with its two neighbouring edges, so that it comes to rest touching the original outline instead of cutting across it. When one end has stayed on an original vertex the other end is instead brought onto the line through the first two original vertices, extended to whichever swallowed vertex lies furthest to the outside.

Every line the grid holds near the candidate is tested, except those sharing an end point with it, which are compared by position and not by identity. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.CalcArea(IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.SimplifyNode},IGS.Genamo.LinkListNode{IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.SimplifyNode})
member.summary: Works out what it would cost to remove a vertex, and writes the answer onto the vertex. A vertex the polygon does not turn outwards at is simply cut off, and costs the area of the triangle it makes with its two neighbours. An outside corner is instead straightened by extending the edge coming into it and the edge leaving the one after it until they meet, which only counts when both neighbours lie on the right side and the two edges meet beyond both their ends; it then costs the area of the triangle that extension adds. Anything else is left at double.MaxValue, meaning the vertex cannot be removed.
member.param: Ring of surviving vertices, used to find the neighbours.
Ring node of the vertex to price.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.CalcArea2(IGS.Genamo.LinkList{IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.SimplifyNode},IGS.Genamo.LinkListNode{IGS.Genamo.PolygonSimplification.SimplifyNode},System.Double)
member.summary: Works out what it would cost to remove a vertex under the cheap rule used by Simplify, and writes the answer onto the vertex. The cost is the area of the triangle the vertex makes with its two neighbours, doubled at an outside corner so that those are given up last. There is no extension point and no crossing test here, which is why the result of Simplify can overlap itself. The commented out lines below the code show an earlier measure based on turning angle and edge length.
member.param: Ring of surviving vertices, used to find the neighbours.
Ring node of the vertex to price.
Not used. It was the total length the earlier measure divided by, and only the commented out lines ever read it.

member.summary: Extends two edges past their ends and reports where they meet, but only when the meeting point lies beyond the end of both. Start of the second edge.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.ShapeSimilarity
member.summary: Measures how alike the shapes of two polygons are, whatever their size or how they are turned, using the turning function metric. Each polygon becomes a step function of heading against normalised arc length; the distance between the two is then minimised over every shift along the perimeter and every rotation, which comes down to walking a list of critical events in one pass. The naming and the references to the paper mark this as a port of the published C implementation.

member.summary: Length of the edge in the polygon's own units, before anything is normalised.

member.summary: Where the edge begins along the perimeter, as a fraction of the total length, so the first edge begins at zero.

The accessors take an index past the end and wrap it, adding a full turn to the heading and one to the arc length each time round, which is what lets the comparison run on past the seam without special casing it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.ShapeSimilarity.CalculateInternal(IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,IGS.Genamo.Poly2d,System.Double@)
member.summary: Does the whole similarity measurement on one instance: turns both polys into turning representations, computes the terms of the metric in one pass, fills the event heap and walks it for the smallest value. Only the nodes of the polys are used, so any bulge is treated as a straight edge, and both are taken as closed. The result is the square root of the smallest squared metric found, or zero when that came out negative through rounding.

Second poly.

member.returns: A metric of how similar the polys are, zero for a perfect match.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Polynomial.ToString
member.summary: Builds a readable form of the polynomial, running from the constant term upwards and writing each non zero term as its coefficient followed by x or x to a power. A coefficient that is not a positive real is put in brackets, and one that is exactly one is left out except in the constant term. The plus between terms is only written when the very next coefficient is non zero, so a polynomial with a gap in it, such as one plus two x squared, comes out with those two terms run together.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quad3d.Contains(IGS.Genamo.Point3d)
member.summary: Checks whether a point lies within the four edges of the quad, by testing that it falls on the inside of each edge in turn, measured against the normal of the triangle through the first three corners. Note that this says nothing about the point lying on the quad: the part of the point that stands off the plane cancels out of every one of those tests, so any point in the infinite prism standing on the quad is reported as inside. Like Contains it takes no notice of how far the point stands from the plane.

member.summary: Computes the distance from a point to the quad, but counts a triangle only when the foot of the perpendicular actually lands within it, so a point standing off the side of the quad gets no answer rather than the distance to the nearest edge. Only the first of the two triangles is checked for being degenerate.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quad3d.Distance2(IGS.Genamo.Point3d,IGS.Genamo.Point3d@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Computes the distance from a point to the curved bilinear patch itself rather than to a triangulation of it, by searching the two parameters for the place where the surface normal points straight at the point. The search is a Nelder Mead amoeba of three solutions, started at random inside the unit square and run for at most a hundred rounds. Those bounds only seed the start and are not held to afterwards, and nothing checks that the answer landed on the patch, so the point handed back can lie off it where Eval has carried the surface on past its corners. The random start comes from one shared generator, so two calls with the same input do not give the same answer.
member.param: Point to measure from.
Set to the point found on the patch, which may lie outside it.
Set to how many rounds the search took.
member.returns: The distance from the point given to the point found.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quad3d.DistanceSpecial2(IGS.Genamo.Point3d)
member.summary: Searches the bilinear patch for the point nearest a given one, the same way as Distance2 but measuring the squared distance itself, and reports nothing unless the answer lands strictly inside the patch. Note that the optimizer already hands back the squared distance and it is then squared once more, so the value returned is the distance raised to the fourth power and not a distance. The stop value is zero, an absolute test that never fires, so all fifty rounds are run every time.
member.param: Point to measure from.
member.returns: The fourth power of the distance when the nearest point lies strictly inside the patch, otherwise minus one.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quad3d.dobj2(System.Double[],System.Object)
member.summary: The measure Distance2 makes small: one minus how nearly the surface normal at a parameter position lines up with the direction from there to the target, so it reaches zero where the line meets the surface at a right angle. Taking the size of the dot product means either direction along the normal counts. Note that the direction is normalized before its length is tested, so a target sitting exactly on the surface gives not a number rather than the zero that test was meant to catch.
member.param: The two parameters u and v of the position on the patch.
The point being measured to, passed through by the optimizer. Cast without being checked.
member.returns: One minus the size of the dot product, from zero at a right angle up to one.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quad3d.dobj(System.Double[],System.Object)
member.summary: The measure DistanceSpecial2 makes small: the squared distance from the target to the point on the patch at a parameter position.
member.param: The two parameters u and v of the position on the patch.
The point being measured to, passed through by the optimizer. Cast without being checked.
member.returns: The squared distance between the two points.

member.summary: Gets the exact arc length of the curve from the closed form of the integral rather than by subdivision. A curve whose control point sits halfway between the ends, and which is therefore really a straight line, is caught first and measured end to end. The formula takes the logarithm of a quantity that falls to zero exactly when the curve folds back on itself in a cusp, so such a curve gives infinity or not a number instead of its true length.

member.summary: Approximates the curve by a new polyline lying within roughly tol of it, splitting at the middle wherever the chord strays too far. The result is left open and holds straight segments only. Nothing bounds the recursion, so a tolerance of zero or less never lets a piece be accepted and the call runs until the stack gives out.

member.returns: A new open poly of straight segments, from the start of the curve to its end.

The acceptance test is made twice over the very same point, since the parameter worked out the second time is the one already used, so the second test costs an extra evaluation and can never disagree with the first.

A parameter at or below zero gives an empty curve sitting on the start point followed by the whole curve, and one at or above one gives the whole curve followed by an empty curve on the end point; in both those cases the parts are built from this curve's own points and share them with it, while a cut in between builds the parts from fresh coordinates that share nothing.

member.summary: Computes the point on the curve at a parameter, blending the three points by the usual quadratic weights. Parameters outside zero to one are not clamped and the curve is simply carried on past its ends.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.QuadraticBezier2d.GetParam(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,System.Double)
member.summary: Finds the parameter at which the curve passes through a point, by solving the x equation alone and taking the first root landing between zero and one. When that fails the point is replaced by the nearest point on the curve and the whole thing is tried once more. Because only x is looked at, a curve that doubles back in x, or one standing vertical, can fail even for a point that really does lie on it. ParamAt does the same job and picks between x and y first.
member.param: Point on the curve to find the parameter of.
Not used.
member.returns: The parameter, between zero and one, or zero when no root could be found.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.QuadraticBezier2d.GetPerpendicular(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Finds every place on the curve where it runs at a right angle to the line from a given point, which is where the distance to that point stops changing. That condition is a cubic in the parameter, written out here in full, and only roots between zero and one are kept. The parameters themselves are not reported, only the points.
member.param: Point to measure from.
member.returns: A new list of new points on the curve, one per root in range, in the order the solver gave them. Empty when every such place falls off the ends of the curve.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.QuadraticBezier2d.ParamAt(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Finds the parameter at which the curve passes through a point, solving on whichever of the two axes the end points lie further apart on, so that a curve standing vertical or lying horizontal is still handled. Note that the choice looks only at the end points, so a curve whose ends are level but which swings far the other way is still solved on the axis it doubles back along. Where two roots come out, the one whose point on the curve lies nearest the point given wins. Unlike GetParam the answer is not held to the range zero to one.
member.param: Point on the curve to find the parameter of.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d
member.summary: A quaternion holding a rotation in space: the three components of an axis scaled by the sine of half the angle, together with the cosine of half the angle. All four components are readonly, so a quaternion never changes once made and every operation hands back a new one. Nothing normalizes on the way in, so one can hold something that is not a rotation at all, and only ToMatrix copes with that by dividing through by the squared magnitude.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.X
member.summary: The four components: X, Y and Z are the axis of rotation scaled by the sine of half the angle, and W is the cosine of half the angle. Readonly, so they are fixed for the life of the quaternion.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.Y
member.summary: The four components: X, Y and Z are the axis of rotation scaled by the sine of half the angle, and W is the cosine of half the angle. Readonly, so they are fixed for the life of the quaternion.

member.summary: The four components: X, Y and Z are the axis of rotation scaled by the sine of half the angle, and W is the cosine of half the angle. Readonly, so they are fixed for the life of the quaternion.

member.summary: The four components: X, Y and Z are the axis of rotation scaled by the sine of half the angle, and W is the cosine of half the angle. Readonly, so they are fixed for the life of the quaternion.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.FromAxisAngle(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,System.Double)
member.summary: Creates a new quaternion for a turn of a given angle about a given axis. The axis is normalized first and need not arrive that way; an axis of no length cannot be normalized and gives the identity quaternion, meaning no rotation at all, rather than an error.
member.param: Axis to turn about. Normalized on the way in, so its length does not matter.
Angle to turn by, in radians.
member.returns: A new quaternion of unit length holding that rotation, or the identity when the axis has no length.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.ToMatrix
member.summary: Builds a new matrix doing the same rotation as this quaternion. Every entry is divided by the squared magnitude, so a quaternion that is not of unit length still gives a clean rotation matrix rather than one carrying a scale; a quaternion of all zeros divides by zero and gives infinities. Only the nine rotation entries are written, the rest being left as the identity, so there is no translation. Note that the rotated axes go into the rows and not the columns, which is what the rest of Matrix3d expects, and is why the layout looks transposed against the form usually printed in books.
member.returns: A new matrix holding this rotation, with no translation.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.FromMatrix(IGS.Genamo.Matrix3d)
member.summary: Creates a new quaternion from the rotation part of a matrix, reading only the three by three corner and taking no notice of any translation. Which component is worked out first is chosen from the largest diagonal entry, so the square root is always taken of the largest of the four candidates and the division that follows stays well behaved. The matrix is taken on trust to be a proper rotation: nothing checks for scale or shear, and a matrix carrying either gives a quaternion that means nothing. This undoes ToMatrix exactly, up to the overall sign that a quaternion shares with its negative.
member.param: Matrix to read the rotation from.
member.returns: A new quaternion holding that rotation.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.op_Multiply(IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d,IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d)
member.summary: Multiplies two quaternions by the Hamilton product, which composes the two rotations, and returns the result as a new quaternion. The product does not commute, so a times b and b times a are different rotations.
member.param: Left quaternion.
Right quaternion.
member.returns: A new quaternion holding the product.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.Conjugate
member.summary: Meant to give the conjugate, which for a rotation is the same turn the other way round. As written it hands its values to the constructor in the wrong order: the constructor takes x, y, z and then w, while what is passed is w followed by the three negated axis components. The result therefore carries the scalar part in the x slot and the negated z in the scalar slot, and is the conjugate of nothing. It should be built from the three negated axis components followed by an unchanged w.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.Magnitude
member.summary: Gets the length of the quaternion taken as a vector of its four components. It is one for any quaternion that really is a rotation.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.Normalized
member.summary: Gets a new quaternion of unit length pointing the same way, leaving this one alone. There is no guard on the magnitude, so a quaternion of all zeros divides by zero and comes back holding values that are not numbers.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.ToString
member.summary: Builds a readable form of the quaternion, the four components in the order x, y, z, w separated by commas and each written the way Utilities.FormatReal writes a number.
member.returns: A new string holding the four components.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d.TwistAndSwingDecompose(IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d@,IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d@,IGS.Genamo.TwistMode)
member.summary: Decomposes this quaternion into a twist (rotation by orthagonal axis given by 'mode), and a swing (rotation from plan perpendicular to twist axis). The result can be multiplied qswing*qtwist to get back the original quaternion.
member.param: Set to the turn about the axis chosen by mode, of unit length. When this quaternion is a half turn about an axis at right angles to the chosen one the divisor comes out zero and the components are not numbers.

Set to the turn left over once the twist is taken out. Note that in the ZAxis case one term carries the wrong sign, so for that mode multiplying the two back together does not give this quaternion again; the other two modes do round trip.
Which axis the twist is taken about. Anything other than the x and y cases falls through to the z one.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.TwistMode
member.summary: Which axis TwistAndSwingDecompose takes the twist about, the swing then being whatever is left over in the plane at right angles to it.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Rat64
member.summary: An exact rational number, held as a big integer numerator over a big integer denominator. Every constructor divides both by their greatest common divisor and keeps the sign on the numerator, so two equal rationals always have the same pair of values. Note that the conversion to and from double is implicit both ways, and the one from double rounds to four decimal places, so an ordinary double mixed into an expression quietly throws the exactness away.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Rat64.A

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Rat64.B
member.summary: The denominator, always positive after construction. Public and writable, so a caller can set it to zero or to a negative value, which the rest of the struct does not expect.

Nothing checks the denominator for being zero: the greatest common divisor of a value and zero is that value, so a zero denominator survives reduction and the rational is left holding something over zero.

Denominator. Not checked for being zero.

member.summary: Converts a rational to a double by dividing the numerator by the denominator, both taken to double first. Being implicit, this happens wherever a double is wanted, which is how ToString and GetHashCode work. A numerator or denominator too large for a double loses precision, and a zero denominator gives infinity or not a number.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Rat64.op_Implicit(System.Double)~IGS.Genamo.Rat64
member.summary: Converts a double to a rational by multiplying by ten thousand and truncating, so the result is the nearest multiple of one ten thousandth below the value and everything finer than that is lost. Being implicit, this happens silently wherever a rational is wanted, which means an ordinary double dropped into an expression quietly throws away the exactness the type exists for. A value above about nine times ten to the fourteenth overflows the cast without a word.
member.param: Value to convert.
member.returns: A new rational holding that value rounded down to a multiple of one ten thousandth.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BigInt.ToFloat64

member.summary: Divides one magnitude by another, giving both the quotient and the remainder. A single digit divisor is handled directly; anything larger goes through the usual long division, lining both up first, guessing each quotient digit from the top two digits and correcting it where the guess was one too large. When the value is smaller than the divisor the quotient is a single zero and the remainder is the value's own array, handed back without being copied.

Digits of the value to divide by.
Set to a new array holding the quotient.
Set to the remainder, which may be a new array or the array given as u.

Big integer to divide by.
Set to a new big integer holding the remainder.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.BigInt.ModPow(System.Int32,IGS.Genamo.BigInt)

member.summary: Computes a LU substitution for this matrix using array v. Returns an array with results and also.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.RealMatrix.Solve(System.Double[])
member.summary: Solves the linear system given by thes matrix (which must be square) using LU decomposition. The arary v has to have the same length as the size of this matrix. If no solution to the system could be found, null is returned.
member.param: The right hand side of the system. Must be as long as the matrix has rows. Left alone, since the work is done on a copy.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.RealPolynomial
member.summary: A polynomial in one variable with real coefficients, with arithmetic, evaluation and root finding on top of it. Note the two orders in play: the constructor takes its coefficients highest power first, the way a polynomial is written, while the indexer and everything inside work from the constant term upwards. Roots come from the exact formulas up to the fourth degree and from a numeric search above that.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.RealPolynomial.SolveCubic(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes the real solutions of a x cubed plus b x squared plus c x plus d equals zero, by the trigonometric and Cardano forms. When c divided by a is not a finite number, which is how a leading coefficient of exactly zero shows itself, the problem is handed to the quadratic solver instead; a leading coefficient that is merely very small is not caught that way. A triple root is reported once rather than three times, and the roots come back in the order the formula produces them rather than sorted.

Coefficient of x squared.
Coefficient of x.
Constant term.
Tolerance handed on to the quadratic solver when this falls back to it. It is not used anywhere else in the method. Defaults to Calc.Epsilon.
member.returns: A new array holding one or three real roots, or whatever the quadratic solver gave when it fell back.

member.param: Coefficient of x to the fourth.
Coefficient of x cubed.
Coefficient of x squared.
Coefficient of x.
Constant term.
How near zero the intermediate terms have to be to count as zero, and the tolerance handed on to the cubic and quadratic solvers. Defaults to Calc.Epsilon.
member.returns: A new array of the real roots, from none up to four of them, unsorted. It never returns null, whatever the summary says. Note the fault in the branch taken when the absolute term comes out at zero: the cubic it then solves is given a constant term of one instead of the term the comment above it names, so the roots that branch returns are wrong.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.RealPolynomial.NumericFindRoots(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Finds the real roots by searching rather than by formula, which is what carries the polynomials above the fourth degree. The extremes of the curve are found first, by calling this on the derivative, and those split the range that can hold roots into stretches over which the curve only rises or only falls; each stretch is then handed to a Brent search. Because a stretch only yields a root where the curve crosses the axis, a root the curve merely touches is missed.
member.param: How closely a root has to be pinned down. The search on the derivative uses a fixed tolerance of its own rather than this one.
How near zero a value has to be to count as a root.
member.returns: A new array of the roots found, in increasing order. Empty when there are none.

How closely a root has to be pinned down by the numeric search.
How near zero a value has to be to count as a root in the numeric search.
member.returns: A new array of the roots found. Empty when there are none, and never null.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d
member.summary: Interpolates a vector of values across the plane from scattered samples. Samples are added one at a time, each carrying a position and however many values belong to it, and asking for a position hands those values back blended. Three samples or more are triangulated and the answer comes from the barycentric weights of the triangle nearest the query, with one and two samples handled as special cases. The triangulation is thrown away and built again whenever a sample is added.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.sampledPoints
member.summary: The samples in the order they were added, each a point in the plane carrying its own array of values.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.triangleLUT
member.summary: The triangles filed by position, so a query can be narrowed to the few that might hold it. Null until it is built and set back to null whenever a sample is added. Note that the point lookup it is searched with is transposed inside ExtentsGrid2d, so it nearly always comes back empty and the search falls through to walking the whole list instead.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.triangleList
member.summary: The same triangles as a plain list, which is what the search walks when nothing is found by position. Null until it is built and set back to null whenever a sample is added.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.minSampleValues
member.summary: The smallest value each component takes across all the samples. The interpolated answer is held up to these, so that a badly shaped triangle cannot push a component below anything ever measured. Built along with the triangles.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.maxSampleValues
member.summary: The largest value each component takes across all the samples, used the same way as the smallest to hold the interpolated answer inside the range the samples actually cover. Built along with the triangles.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.AddSample(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double[])
member.summary: Adds one sample at a position, with as many values as the caller cares to give, and throws away the triangulation so the next interpolation builds it again. The array of values is stored by reference and not copied, so an array the caller keeps and later changes changes the sample with it. Nothing checks for two samples landing on the same position.
member.param: X of the sample position.
Y of the sample position.
The values belonging to this position. Stored by reference.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.Interpolate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes the values at a position by blending the samples around it. With no samples at all it throws, with one it hands back a copy of that sample's values, and with two it interpolates along the line between them. From three samples upwards the samples are triangulated once and the answer comes from the barycentric weights of the triangle nearest the position, so a position outside every triangle is extrapolated from the nearest one rather than refused. The weights are not held to the triangle, and what keeps that extrapolation from running away is the last step, which holds every component inside the range the samples cover. Where samples carry different numbers of values the answer is only as long as the shortest of the three corners, so its length can depend on where the query lands.
member.param: X of the position to interpolate at.
Y of the position to interpolate at.
member.returns: A new array of the interpolated values.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.CopyArray(System.Double[])
member.summary: Makes a copy of an array, so that what is handed out to a caller is never one of the sample arrays itself. It reads nothing from the instance, so it could as well be static.
member.param: Array to copy.
member.returns: A new array holding the same values.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.FindClosestTriangle(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Finds the triangle to interpolate in for a position. The grid is asked first for the triangles whose boxes hold the position; a single answer is taken as it stands, without checking that the position really falls inside that triangle, while several are narrowed down by distance. When the grid finds nothing, and it nearly always finds nothing because of the transposed cell lookup in ExtentsGrid2d, every triangle is measured instead, which makes each query cost a walk over the whole list.
member.param: Position to find a triangle for.
member.returns: The triangle nearest the position, or null when there are no triangles at all, which the caller does not check for.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.RegenerateTriangleLUT
member.summary: Triangulates the samples and builds both the grid and the plain list from the result, together with the smallest and largest value each component takes. A triangle whose area does not reach 0.001 is left out as too thin to interpolate across. Note that this limit is an absolute one rather than a share of the sample bounds, so on data measured in small units it can throw every triangle away and leave nothing to interpolate in at all. The grid cells are a twentieth of the longer side of the sample bounds. The count of triangles dropped is kept but never read again.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.SampleBounds
member.summary: Gets a new box covering the positions of all the samples. It is worked out afresh on every read, and only the triangulation reads it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.Interpolate2Samples(System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.SamplePoint,IGS.Genamo.SampleInterpolator2d.SamplePoint)
member.summary: Function used to interpolate sample when only 2 data points is added.
member.param: X of the position to interpolate at.
Y of the position to interpolate at.
First sample, which the position is projected onto the line from.
Second sample, at the far end of that line.
member.returns: A new array of the interpolated values. Note that when the position falls beyond either end the values come from the first or second sample of the list rather than from the two handed in, which agree only because the one caller passes exactly those two.

member.summary: One sample: a point in the plane that also carries the values measured there. It derives from Point2d so the triangulation and the geometry can treat it as an ordinary point while the values ride along, which is how a triangle hands the values of its corners back.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Set`1.GetHashCode

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1
member.summary: General purpose skiplist class. A skiplist is a sorted linked list with O(logn) search time. The skiplist works like a binary tree but also have linear traversal access to the sorted elements.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.cnt
member.summary: How many values are in the list, not counting the two sentinels. It is kept by hand as nodes are added and erased rather than counted, so erasing a node that was never in this list leaves it wrong.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.rnd
member.summary: The source of the coin tosses that decide how tall each new node is. There is one per list, seeded the way the framework seeds a new generator, so two lists made at the same moment can end up with the same run of heights. That only affects how well balanced they come out, not what they hold.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.prob
member.summary: The chance that a node reaches one level higher than the last, so a half means about half as many nodes on each level as on the one below it. Changing it only affects nodes added afterwards.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.compare
member.summary: The comparison the list is sorted by, either the one handed to the constructor or, by default, one that casts each value to the non generic IComparable. Add always uses this one; Find has an overload that takes a different comparison for a single search.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.head
member.summary: The sentinel standing before the first value. It carries no value of its own, its arrays are the full 128 long whatever the list's height, and its Height says how many levels are currently in use. Internal so the enumerator can tell the start of the list apart from a real node.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.tail
member.summary: The sentinel standing after the last value, which is what the End property hands out as the one past the end marker. It carries no value and its forward links are never set, so nothing may step past it. Internal so the enumerator can recognise the end.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SkipList`1.RandomHeight
member.summary: Tosses a coin repeatedly to decide how many levels a new node takes part in. The chance of going one higher each time is the probability of the list, so most nodes come out one level tall and each level above holds a shrinking share of them. It never returns more than 128, which is how tall the two sentinels are built.
member.returns: A height from one up to 128.

member.summary: Walks the values of a skip list in sorted order, along the bottom level of links only. It holds the list by reference and keeps no record of how many times the list has changed, so adding or erasing while a walk is running is not caught and leaves the walk following whatever the links now say.

member.summary: The node the walk stands on. It starts at the list's head sentinel, meaning before the first value, and reaches the tail sentinel once the last value has been passed.

member.summary: The list being walked, held by reference so that its two sentinels can be recognised.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SkipListEnumerator`1.#ctor(IGS.Genamo.SkipList{`0})
member.summary: Creates a new walk standing before the first value of a list. MoveNext has to be called once before Current can be read.
member.param: List to walk. Held by reference.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SkipListEnumerator`1.Reset
member.summary: Puts the walk back before the first value, so the list can be gone over again.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.SkipListEnumerator`1.Current
member.summary: Gets the value the walk stands on, as an object, so a value type is boxed on every read. Reading it before the first MoveNext throws, but reading it after MoveNext has reported the end does not: the walk then stands on the tail sentinel and its default value comes back with nothing to say so.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SkipListEnumerator`1.MoveNext
member.summary: Steps on to the next value, starting at the first one when the walk has not begun. Note that it is only sound to call while it keeps saying yes: once it has reported the end the walk stands on the tail sentinel, whose forward link was never set, so a further call steps on to nothing at all and reports yes again.
member.returns: True while there is a value to read, false once the last one has been passed.

member.remarks: This method checks if two line segments, defined by their endpoints, intersect by calculating intersection parameters (s and t) and ensures that the intersection lies on both segments. member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.SpanGrid
member.summary: A raster of occupied cells stored one row at a time as a sorted list of disjoint x intervals, which makes a large but mostly empty shape far cheaper to hold and to test than a full bitmap. It is built by scan converting polygons at a chosen cell size and is used for nesting: two grids can be tested for collision, and a part can be swept into the first free place. Positions are in whole cells; Pos says where the grid's own lower left corner sits in that same cell space.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.SpanGrid.Interval
member.summary: A run of set cells on one row, from x1 to x2 with both ends counted. The comparison it carries is not an ordering in the usual sense: two runs that touch or overlap compare equal, which is what lets a binary search find the run a new one has to be merged with.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.SpanGrid.Interval.x2
member.summary: Rightmost cell of the run, counted in, so a run of one cell has both ends the same.

member.summary: Widens this run to cover both itself and another, in place, so it reaches from the leftmost of the two ends to the rightmost. Any gap between them is swallowed as well, which is only sound when the caller already knows the two touch or overlap.

member.summary: Orders this run against another for the benefit of a binary search. Note that zero here means the two touch or overlap rather than that they are equal, as the note in the body says, so this is not a proper ordering and sorting a list of runs with it only behaves while they are all disjoint. Anything that is not a run gives a null reference error.
member.param: The other run to compare against. Must be an Interval.
member.returns: Minus one when this run ends before the other begins, one when it begins after the other ends, and zero when the two overlap.
