member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SpanGrid.CreateGrid.CreateSpanGrid(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Poly2d},System.Double)
member.summary: Scan converts a list of polygons into per row crossings. The cell box is worked out from the combined bounding box, one empty list is made per row, every poly is scanned in, and each row's two lists are sorted at the end so that the crossings pair up left to right.

member.summary: Scan converts one poly into per row crossings, handing an open one straight to AddOpen. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SpanGrid.ScanContour
member.summary: Traces the outline of the set cells and returns it as a closed poly in cell coordinates, by walking the boundary and turning as far left as it can at every step. It seeds from a run it finds by scanning the rows, but the search keeps going after it finds one, so the seed is taken from the highest row with a run rather than the lowest. The walk ends when it comes back to where it started and nothing else bounds it, so a shape it cannot walk round leaves it going.

That means a search leaves the grid holding run lengths rather than set flags, and it cannot be asked what is set afterwards.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.SpatialIndex2d.Finish
member.summary: Packs the boxes into the tree, which has to be done once after the last Add and before any query. When there are no more items than fit in one node the sorting is skipped and a single root box covering everything is written. Otherwise each box's centre is mapped onto a grid of 65535 by 65535, turned into a position along a Hilbert curve, and the boxes are sorted by that, which puts boxes that lie near each other near each other in the array; the levels above are then filled in bottom up, one parent per run of node size children. Note that the mapping divides by the width and the height of the overall box with no check, so a set of items all at one x or all at one y divides by zero and the ordering comes out meaningless. Nothing stops this being called twice, which would run off the end of the arrays.

member.summary: Cuts a poly into pieces that each run monotonically in y, so that no piece turns back on itself vertically. Arcs are first split at their own topmost and bottommost points, then the nodes are walked and a new piece is started at every node that is a local minimum or maximum, comparing points by y and then by x. A closed poly is walked from its lowest node so that the first and the last piece do not have to be joined afterwards. The input poly is not modified; the pieces are new polys. member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Triangle2d.Contains(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Checks if a point lies inside the triangle by testing the sign of the cross product against each of the three edges and requiring the three signs to agree. That makes the test work for either winding order, and it is inclusive: a point exactly on an edge or on a corner gives a cross product of 0 and counts as inside. No tolerance is applied, so the boundary case rests on the exact floating point sign. A degenerate triangle whose corners are distinct but collinear reports true for any point on that line and false everywhere else, but one whose three corners coincide gives a cross product of 0 for every point in the plane and so reports true for all of them.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d.Normal
member.summary: Gets the normal of the triangle plane as a new unit vector, taken as p1 to p3 crossed with p1 to p2. That is the reverse of the right hand rule read over p1, p2, p3, so the normal points away from the viewer for a triangle whose corners run counter clockwise on screen. A degenerate triangle, whose cross product is shorter than epsilon, is returned without being normalised, so the result is then a near zero vector rather than a unit one.

member.summary: Computes the point of the triangle nearest a given point, by deciding which corner region, edge region or the face itself the point falls into and answering from that region alone. Follows the algorithm in 'Real time collision detection' page 141. A point off the plane is handled as well as one in it, since the face case projects the point onto the plane.

member.returns: The projected line

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d.Contains(IGS.Genamo.Point3d)
member.summary: Checks if a point lies inside the triangle, by taking the cross product along each of the three edges and demanding that none of them points against the face normal. Only the part of the point lying in the triangle plane counts, so a point above or below the face is judged on where it projects. The normal used here is p1 to p2 crossed with p1 to p3, which points the opposite way to the Normal property, but since the same vector is used in all three tests the answer is unaffected. No tolerance is applied, so a point exactly on an edge counts as inside.
member.param: Point to test.
member.returns: true when the point projects inside or onto an edge of the triangle, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d.Intersects(IGS.Genamo.Extents3d)
member.summary: Checks if the triangle overlaps an axis aligned box, using the separating axis theorem. The box is conceptually moved to the origin and the triangle moved with it, then the nine axes formed by crossing each box axis with each triangle edge are tried, followed by the three box axes themselves and finally the triangle plane against the box. As soon as one of those axes separates the two the test gives up and reports no overlap. Touching counts as overlapping.
member.param: Box to test against.
member.returns: true when the triangle and the box overlap, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Triangle3d.TestAxis(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,System.Double,System.Double,System.Double,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d)
member.summary: Tests one of the nine cross product axes for Intersects(). Projects the box half extents and the three triangle corners onto the axis formed by crossing u with f, and checks whether the two projections overlap. A zero length axis, which happens when u and f are parallel, gives a radius and three projections all of zero and so counts as no separation.
member.param: Box axis to cross with the triangle edge.
Triangle edge vector to cross with the box axis.
First box axis, used to project the box onto the test axis.
Second box axis, used to project the box onto the test axis.
Third box axis, used to project the box onto the test axis.
Half extent of the box along u0.
Half extent of the box along u1.
Half extent of the box along u2.
First triangle corner, measured from the box centre.
Second triangle corner, measured from the box centre.
Third triangle corner, measured from the box centre.
member.returns: false when this axis separates the triangle from the box, true when it does not and the test is inconclusive.

member.name: P:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.Item(System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets or sets a component by index, 0 for x, 1 for y and 2 for z. The index is reduced with the C# remainder operator rather than Calc.Mod, and that operator truncates toward zero, so a negative index does not wrap the way it does elsewhere in the library: -1 and -2 both give z, and only -3, -6 and so on reach x. Keep the index in the range 0 to 2.

A surface normal under non uniform scaling needs GetTransformedNormal instead, since this will not keep it perpendicular to its surface.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.Transform(IGS.Genamo.Quaternion3d)

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.Angle(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d)
member.summary: Computes the inner angle between this vector and another
member.param: The other vector.
member.returns: The unsigned angle in radians, between zero and PI. Returns zero when either vector has zero length, which is indistinguishable from a real zero angle.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.DiffrentialAngle(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,IGS.Genamo.Vector3d)
member.summary: Returns the signed angle in range (-PI,PI) from this vector to vector v, in the plane that has 'normal' as normal. The normal is needed because we dont know which side of the plane defined by the vectors that is frontside. 'normal' does not need to be normalized.
member.param: The vector the angle is measured to.
The normal of the plane the angle is measured in. It need not be normalized, but it must be longer than about 1e-6 or the method gives up.
member.returns: The signed angle in radians. Returns zero when the normal is too short to use, which is indistinguishable from a real zero angle; passing this.Cross(v) as the normal hits that case whenever the two vectors are parallel or antiparallel.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.NormalizeIfNeededAndPossible(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d@,System.Double)
member.summary: Normalizes the vector if needed (if not already length=1) If vectors squared length is less than zerotol, false is returned and v is untouched. If vectors squared length is 1 (using zerotol for fuzz), true is returned and v is untouched. Otherwise v is normalized and true is returned.
member.param: The vector to normalize. It is replaced with a new normalized vector rather than being modified, so the caller's own object is never changed.
The tolerance used on the squared length, both for deciding the vector is already unit and for rejecting it as too short.
member.returns: True when v can be used as a unit vector, false when it is too short.

The axis to rotate about.
True to normalize the axis first. Pass false only for an axis already known to be of unit length, because a longer axis silently scales and skews the result.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.Interpolate(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d,System.Double)
member.summary: Computes a linear blend between this vector and another as a new vector. Because the blend is linear rather than angular, a value halfway between two unit vectors is shorter than one unit, so renormalize the result when a direction is wanted. Values outside 0 to 1 extrapolate beyond the two ends.
member.param: The vector reached at a parameter of one.
The blend parameter, zero for this vector and one for end.
member.returns: A new vector holding the blend.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.Bisector(IGS.Genamo.Vector3d)
member.summary: Computes the vector that is the bisector of this and another vector. The length of the result is undefined. If any of the two input vectors has zero length, the result is the other input vector.
member.param: The other vector.
member.returns: A new vector bisecting the two, built as the sum of the two normalized inputs, so its length runs from zero to two. Two vectors pointing in opposite directions give the zero vector, which carries no direction at all.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vector3d.DistanceToXYPlane(System.Double)
member.summary: Computes how far the vector travels through a slab of material of the given thickness, measured along the vector itself. This is thickness divided by the cosine of the angle to straight down, so it is only meaningful for a downward pointing direction: a vector tilted past horizontal returns a negative distance, and a horizontal one returns an enormous but finite number rather than infinity, because the cosine of the computed right angle is not exactly zero. An exception is thrown if the vector has zero length.
member.param: The thickness of the material.
member.returns: The slant distance through the material.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin
member.summary: Joins loose line segments into closed polys. Segments are added one at a time, their end points are merged where they coincide, and Compute then walks the resulting graph picking the sharpest clockwise turn at every node so that each walk closes a single face. Used by Vornoi2d.Cells to turn a set of Voronoi edges into cell polygons.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode
member.summary: A shared end point of one or more edges. Nodes compare equal when they are within Calc.Epsilon of each other, which is what lets MergeNodes weld coincident ends together.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode.pt
member.summary: The position of the node.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode.edges
member.summary: Every edge that meets at this node. Filled by Add and extended by MergeNodes when another node is welded into this one.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode.#ctor
member.summary: Creates a new node with no position and no edges. The position is set by the first call to Add.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode.#ctor(IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode)
member.summary: Copy constructor. The point is taken over by reference and the edge list is shared rather than copied, so the new node and the original see each other's edges.
member.param: The node to copy.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode.Add(IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Attaches an edge to this node and moves the node onto the chosen end of that edge. The point is copied, the edge is not. Calling this a second time moves the node again, so the last call wins.
member.param: The edge to attach.
True to sit the node on the edge start point, false for the end point.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinNode.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Compares two nodes by position, treating any two within Calc.Epsilon as the same node. Because that equality is not transitive, three nodes strung out at just under epsilon apart can compare inconsistently, and a sort using this order is not guaranteed stable in that case. Throws if the object is not a JoinNode.
member.param: The node to compare with.
member.returns: Zero when the two are within Calc.Epsilon, otherwise the ordering of the two points.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge.start
member.summary: The node at the start of the segment. Null until Add wires it up, and repointed by MergeNodes when nodes are welded.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge.end
member.summary: The node at the end of the segment. Null until Add wires it up, and repointed by MergeNodes when nodes are welded.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge.used
member.summary: True once the walk has taken this edge, so it is not used again.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge.#ctor(IGS.Genamo.Line2d)
member.summary: Creates a new edge from a line. The line is copied, so later changes to the argument do not reach the edge.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge.#ctor(IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge)
member.summary: Copy constructor. Note that the line is copied from this edge's own field rather than from the edge passed in, and that field is still null at this point, so the call throws. Nothing in the file calls this constructor.
member.param: The edge to copy.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.edges
member.summary: Every edge added so far. Compute empties this list as it walks.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.nodes
member.summary: Every end point added so far, two per edge until MergeNodes welds the coincident ones.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.region
member.summary: The region the closed polys are collected into. This is what Compute returns.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.Add(IGS.Genamo.Line2d)
member.summary: Adds geometry to join.

member.summary: Joins the geometry added with the Add functions.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.Join(IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge)
member.summary: Walks the graph from one edge, following the sharpest clockwise turn at each node until the path returns to its start, and adds the closed poly to the region. Every edge taken is flagged as used. A walk that runs out of edges before closing is discarded.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.SelectNext(IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.JoinEdge)
member.summary: Picks the edge to follow after a given one. Of the unused edges leaving the far node, it takes the one making the smallest clockwise turn from the reversed direction of travel, which is what keeps a walk hugging one face. The edge straight back along the same pair of nodes is skipped.

member.returns: The next edge to follow, or null when no unused edge leaves that node.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.CellJoin.MergeNodes
member.summary: Welds nodes that lie within Calc.Epsilon of each other. The list is sorted first and only neighbouring entries are compared, so coincident nodes that do not end up adjacent in that order are not merged. Edges of a merged node are repointed at the surviving node.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Edge
member.summary: One directed edge of a quad-edge subdivision, as described by Guibas and Stolfi. Four Edge objects make up a QuadEdge: two opposite directions of the primal edge and two of its dual. The navigation methods below move between edges without any geometry being consulted, so the whole triangulation is traversed by pointer chasing.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Edge.qedge
member.summary: The QuadEdge this edge is one of the four parts of.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Edge.next
member.summary: The next edge counter clockwise around the origin of this one. Rewired by Splice.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Edge.pt
member.summary: The origin point of the edge. Held by reference, so two edges can share one point object.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Edge.idx
member.summary: Which of the four slots of the QuadEdge this edge occupies, 0 to 3. The navigation methods work by stepping this index around that group of four.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Edge.node
member.summary: The node holding this edge in the owning Vornoi2d edge list, so it can be removed in constant time. Null for dual edges, which are never put in that list.

member.returns: The dual edge one step back.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.Sym

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.OPrev

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.DNext

member.returns: The next edge around the destination.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.DPrev

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.LNext

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.LPrev

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.RNext

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.RPrev
member.summary: Gets the previous edge about the face to the right of this one. Nothing in the file calls this.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.Org

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.Dest

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.Org2d
member.summary: Gets the origin of the edge as the point object the subdivision holds, not a copy. Writing to the result moves every edge sharing that point.

member.summary: Gets the destination of the edge as the point object the subdivision holds, not a copy. Writing to the result moves every edge sharing that point.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.EndPoints(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d)

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.MakeEdge
member.summary: Creates a new isolated edge, by building a QuadEdge and handing back its first slot. The edge has no end points yet; call EndPoints to place it.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.DeleteEdge(IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Detaches an edge from the subdivision by splicing it out of the rings at both of its ends. The edge is not removed from any owning edge list, so a caller keeping one must do that separately. Only the commented out branch of Vornoi2d.Insert calls this.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Edge.Splice(IGS.Genamo.Edge,IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Joins or splits the edge rings around the origins of two edges, and independently the rings around their left faces. If the two rings are separate this merges them; if they are the same ring it breaks it in two. This is the single primitive every other structural change in the file is built from.

The second edge.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.QuadEdge
member.summary: A group of four Edge objects making up one edge of a quad-edge subdivision: slots 0 and 2 are the two directions of the primal edge, slots 1 and 3 the two directions of its dual. Navigating between them is what Rot, InvRot and Sym do.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.QuadEdge.edges
member.summary: The four edges of the group, indexed by the idx each one carries.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.QuadEdge.#ctor
member.summary: Creates a new group of four edges and wires them into the standard starting arrangement: a primal edge that is its own next edge at both ends, crossed by a dual edge whose two halves point at each other. The edges have no end points until EndPoints is called.

member.name: T:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d
member.summary: Builds a Delaunay triangulation of a set of points with the Guibas and Stolfi incremental algorithm, and derives the Voronoi diagram from it as the dual. The whole triangulation is computed by the constructor; the query methods only read it. Note the class name is spelled Vornoi rather than Voronoi. Nothing in the product constructs this type at present, the two call sites in CommandCutoff and CommandPatrik both being commented out.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.startedge
member.summary: The edge Locate starts its walk from. Moved to the last located edge after every insert, so that points inserted near each other are found quickly.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.ea
member.summary: The bottom edge of the enclosing super triangle. Its end points are not input points and the query methods filter out anything touching them.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.eb
member.summary: The right edge of the enclosing super triangle.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.ec
member.summary: The left edge of the enclosing super triangle.

member.name: F:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.edges
member.summary: Every primal edge of the subdivision. Dual edges are reachable through Rot but are never put in this list.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.#ctor(System.Collections.Generic.List{IGS.Genamo.Point2d})
member.summary: Creates a new triangulation of the given points. A super triangle large enough to enclose the bounding box is built first, then every point is inserted into it in the order given. The points are stored by reference rather than copied. An empty list still produces the super triangle, built around an empty bounding box.
member.param: The points to triangulate.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Lines(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Collects the edges of either the triangulation or its dual as line segments. Edges touching a corner of the enclosing super triangle are left out, so the result covers only the input points. The Voronoi form joins the circumcentres of the two triangles either side of each edge, so it needs three distinct points on both sides and will throw or give a degenerate centre where that does not hold.
member.param: True for the Voronoi edges, false for the Delaunay edges.
member.returns: A new list of new lines.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Circles
member.summary: Collects the circumcircle of the triangle to the left of each edge, skipping edges that touch a corner of the enclosing super triangle. Nothing calls this.
member.returns: A new list of circumcircles, one per surviving edge rather than one per triangle.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Triangles
member.summary: Collects the triangle to the left of each edge as a closed three node poly, skipping any triangle with a corner on the enclosing super triangle. The result has one entry per surviving edge, so a triangle reachable from more than one of its edges appears more than once.
member.returns: A new list of new closed polys.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Cells
member.summary: Builds the Voronoi cells as closed polys, by feeding every dual edge to CellJoin twice, once in each direction, so that a walk can close a face from either side. Nothing calls this.
member.returns: The polys of the joined region. This is the region's own list, not a copy.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Insert(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Inserts one point into the triangulation and restores the Delaunay property around it, by connecting the point to the corners of the triangle that contains it and then flipping every suspect edge whose opposite vertex falls inside the circumcircle. A point already present within Calc.Epsilon is ignored. The branch handling a point landing exactly on an existing edge is commented out, so such a point is treated as being inside the triangle.
member.param: The point to insert. It is stored by reference.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Connect(IGS.Genamo.Edge,IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Creates a new edge from the destination of one edge to the origin of another, spliced in so that all three share the same left face, and adds it to the edge list.
member.param: The edge whose destination the new edge starts at.
The edge whose origin the new edge ends at.
member.returns: The new edge.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Swap(IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Turns an edge counter clockwise inside the quadrilateral formed by the two triangles that share it, which is the flip that restores the Delaunay property. Works in place on the subdivision.
member.param: The edge to flip.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.TriArea(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Computes twice the signed area of the triangle through three points, which is the standard orientation determinant. Exact sign matters more than the magnitude here.
member.param: The first corner.
The second corner.
The third corner.
member.returns: Twice the area, positive when the three run counter clockwise, negative when clockwise and zero when collinear.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.InCircle(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Checks whether a point lies inside the circle through three other points, using the determinant test from Guibas and Stolfi rather than building the circle. The test assumes the first three are counter clockwise; given clockwise input the answer is inverted. No tolerance is applied, so a point exactly on the circle counts as outside.
member.param: The first point on the circle.
The second point on the circle.
The third point on the circle.
The point to test.
member.returns: True when d lies strictly inside the circle, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.ccw(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Checks whether three points run counter clockwise. Collinear points count as not counter clockwise, with no tolerance applied.
member.param: The first point.
The second point.
The third point.
member.returns: True when the three turn counter clockwise, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.RightOf(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Checks whether a point lies strictly to the right of a directed edge.
member.param: The point to test.
The edge to test against.
member.returns: True when the point is to the right of the edge, otherwise false. A point on the edge line counts as false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.LeftOf(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Checks whether a point lies strictly to the left of a directed edge. Nothing calls this.
member.param: The point to test.
The edge to test against.
member.returns: True when the point is to the left of the edge, otherwise false. A point on the edge line counts as false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.OnEdge(IGS.Genamo.Point2d,IGS.Genamo.Edge)
member.summary: Checks whether a point lies on an edge, by measuring its distance to the segment against Calc.Epsilon. That is an absolute distance rather than one scaled to the model, so it does not hold across very different drawing sizes. Only the commented out branch of Insert calls this.
member.param: The point to test.
The edge to test against.
member.returns: True when the point is within Calc.Epsilon of the segment, otherwise false.

member.name: M:IGS.Genamo.Vornoi2d.Locate(IGS.Genamo.Point2d)
member.summary: Finds an edge of the triangle containing a point, by walking from the last located edge in the general direction of the point. If the point coincides with an end point of an edge within Calc.Epsilon that edge is returned instead. The walk has no iteration guard, so a subdivision left inconsistent by earlier degenerate input can loop here forever.
member.param: The point to locate.
member.returns: An edge the point lies on, or an edge of the triangle containing it.
